rows.output: Fleetwood was the European champion of the four-ball match, having won the Ryder Cup four times, when he and Molinari were paired together as the 'Molliwood' team in the final match of the 2018 Ryder Cup.
rows.reference: Fleetwood is the first European rookie to win four points in a row while he and Molinari, dubbed "Molliwood" after a sensational weekend are only the second pair to win four points from their opening four matches in Ryder Cup history.

rows.source: Léyìn tíwọ́n ti tẹ Woods àti Patrick Reed lórí mọ́lẹ̀ ninu àwọn oníbọ́ọ̀lù-mẹ́rin wọn búgbàmu  pẹ̀lú agbára láti borí Woods tí táyà ẹsẹ̀ rẹ̀ tijò àti ọ̀dọ́ ilẹ̀ Amẹrika tíkòni ìrírí Bryson Dechambeau nípaṣẹ̀ 5 àti 4 tórinlẹ̀ díẹ̀ síi.
rows.output: The Woods and Patrick Reed won the tournament in a playoff with a birdie on the fourth hole, beating Woods' previous record of 11 consecutive birdies and the American record of 10 consecutive birdies by Bryson DeChambeau by 5 and 4 strokes.
rows.reference: Having crushed Woods and Patrick Reed in the fourballs they then gelled superbly to beat a deflated Woods and American rookie Bryson Dechambeau by an even more emphatic 5&4.

rows.source: Woods, ẹnití ó wọ́ ara rẹ̀ kọjà ninu gbogbo àwọn ìdíje méji lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta, fi àwọn ìbújade iṣẹ́ ọpọlọ hàn lẹ́ẹ̀kọ̀kan ṣùgbọ́n nísinsìnyí ó ti pàdánù mọ́kàndínlógún ninu àwọn ìdíje mọ́kàndínlọ́gbọ̀n rẹ̀ ninu àwọn oníbọ́ọ̀lù-mẹ́rin àti àwọn onímẹ́rin àti méje láìdúró.
rows.output: Woods, who was in the lead in both races, won the first race by a margin of 1.2 seconds, and then won the second race by a margin of 1.6 seconds.
rows.reference: Woods, who dragged himself through two matches on Saturday, showed occasional bursts of brilliance but he has now lost 19 of his 29 matches in fourballs and foursomes and seven in a row.

rows.output: Justin Rose, who was in the lead after three rounds, was overtaken by a group of four, including fellow Englishman Henrik Stenson, who finished two strokes ahead of Dustin Johnson and Brooks Koepka - the two-time defending champion.

rows.output: Europe was in a state of shock, and the people were in a state of panic, as the news of the attack on the city of Paris spread throughout the continent.

rows.output: Geiger counter is a device used to measure the level of radiation. It is a type of radiation detector that is used to measure the level of radiation in the environment. The device is named after its inventor, Hans Geiger, who developed it in the 1920s.

rows.output: The path to the development of a monoclonal antibody drug, such as trastuzumab, is a long and arduous one. It begins with the identification of a target, such as the HER2 protein, which is overexpressed in certain types of cancer. The drug is then designed to bind to this target and block its function. In the case of trastuzumab, the drug binds to the HER2 protein and prevents it from interacting with other proteins that promote cell growth. This prevents the growth of cancer cells that rely on the HER2 protein for their growth.
rows.reference: The method involves extracting immune cells from a patient, altering them in the laboratory so they can "see" a protein common to many cancers called HER2, and then reinjecting the cells.

rows.output: A computer programmer, who had been working on a top-secret project for the British government, was found dead in a locked room in the Ministry of Defence, apparently having committed suicide, with a note in his hand, which, when read, revealed that he had been working on a top-secret project to develop a new type of nuclear weapon, and that he had been killed by a group of government officials who were trying to cover up the project.
rows.reference: A cyber-hacker has infiltrated Britain's super-secret web network of spies, revealing the identities of all Britain's agents in the field, to the dismay of the agent on duty - a regrettably small role for Kevin Eldon.

rows.source: Ó jẹ́ ohun tóba gbogbo ọ̀rọ̀ jẹ́ fún adarí ìgbìmọ̀ ìjọbà ẹnití ó jẹ́ àwòrán ológe àti ẹnití ogun ńjà kan, tó ńjìyà ìyọ́bí-òrí pátápátá ti òṣèlú tíkò gbajúmọ̀: Emma Thompson ṣe ohun tí ó dára jùlọ tí o leè ṣe pẹ́lù ìwà tí kòfi-gbogbo-arajọti-Teresa-May ṣùgbọ́n kòsí nǹkan púpọ̀ ninu àkọsílẹ̀ eré náà láti ṣiṣ̵ẹ́ pẹ̀lú.
rows.output: He was a man of great honor and integrity, a man who was a symbol of hope and strength to the people, and a man who was a warrior in the fight against poverty and inequality. Emma Thompson did a great job of capturing the essence of this man, who was a true leader and a champion of the people.
rows.reference: It's the last straw for a prime minister who is a pompous and embattled figure, already suffering a complete meltdown of political unpopularity: Emma Thompson does her very best with this quasi-Teresa-May character but there's nothing much in the script to work with.

rows.source: Àwọn olùdámọ̀ràn iṣẹ́ ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ rẹ̀ sọ fún un pé níwọn ìgbàtí ìkọ̀ọ̀kan ninu àwọn àmì ti gbọ̀jẹ̀gẹ́, yóò nílò láti mú ẹnìkan wá láti inu ìfẹ̀yìntì.
rows.output: The elders of the land will be summoned to testify against him, and he will be put to death by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
rows.reference: Her intelligence advisers inform her that as every single active spy has been compromised, she will have to bring someone out of retirement.

rows.source: Àtipé ìyẹn túmọ̀ si Johnny English aláìlọ́wọ́ fúnrarẹ̀, tíwọn ti fún níṣẹ́ bíi ọ̀gá ilé ìwé nílé iṣẹ́ tódùn un wò kan, ṣùgbọ́n fífún ni àwọn ẹ̀kọ́ aílàlákọsílẹ̀ nipa bí a ti ńjẹ́ òṣìṣẹ́ ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ̀ kan: àwọn ẹ̀fẹ̀ apanilẹ́ẹ̀rín níbí, bí English sooe ńfúnni ni irúfẹ́-Ilé-ìwé-ti-Àpáta ilé ẹ̀kọ́ ti amí ṣíṣe.
rows.output: Johnny English, who was once a bumbling government employee, has now been appointed as the head of the Ministry of Magic. He is now in a position to make decisions that will affect the entire wizarding world, and he is not taking it lightly. The Ministry of Magic is a place where magic is used for both good and evil, and Johnny English is aware of the potential dangers that come with it.
rows.reference: And that means bumbling Johnny English himself, now employed as a schoolmaster in some posh establishment, but giving off-the-record lessons in how to be an undercover operative: some nice gags here, as English offers a School of Rock-type academy of spying.

rows.source: English níwọn ti gbé padà ní kíákía sí Whitehall fún ìbanisọ̀rọ̀ pàjáwìrì tí ó sì túnwà níṣọ̀kan pẹ̀lú ọ̀rẹ́ tímọ́tímọ́ tóńjìyà fúngbà pípẹ́ Bough, tí wọn ṣe eré rẹ̵̀ lẹ́ẹ́kan síi láti ọwọ́ Ben Miller.
rows.output: They have returned to Whitehall to protest against the government's decision to cut funding for the arts, which has been criticized by many, including the actor Ben Miller.
rows.reference: English is whisked back to Whitehall for an emergency briefing and reunited with his former long-suffering sidekick Bough, played again by Ben Miller.

rows.source: Bough ní báyìí ti dí ọkùnrin tóti gbéyàwó kan, tíwọn sọ mọ́ balógun ọko ogun abẹ́-omi kan, ipa àwọn igi bọ́ọ̀lú-àfigigbá onídùnnú kan ninu eyiti wọn ti fi Vicki Pepperdine ṣòfo díẹ̀.
rows.output: Bough was a young man who had been a soldier, and he was now a captain of a merchant ship. He had a large family, and he had been married to Vicki Pepperdine.
rows.reference: Bough is now a married man, hitched to a submarine commander, a jolly-hockey-sticks role in which Vicki Pepperdine is a bit wasted.

rows.source: Nítorínáà Batman àti Robin ti mimu àwọn nǹkan mẹ̀hẹ gidigidi níbi Iṣ̵ẹ́ Ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ̵́ ti Ọbabìnrin Ọlọ́lá Jùlọ ti padà sẹnu iṣẹ́, tíwọn sì ńṣe aláàbápàdé obìnrin àrẹwà amúniṣagbère Ophelia Bulletova ti Olgs Kurylenko.
rows.output: Because Batman and Robin have been doing a lot of things in the wrong places, the wrong people have come to the wrong places, and the wrong people have come to the wrong places.
rows.reference: So the Batman and Robin of getting things terribly wrong on Her Majesty's Secret Service are back in action, encountering Olga Kurylenko's beautiful femme fatale Ophelia Bulletova.

rows.source: Ẹwẹ, adarí ìgbìmọ̀ ìjọba ǹsubú lọ́nà tóléwu lábẹ̵́ èèdì ti ọlọ̀pọ̀-èrò oníṣẹ́ ìmọ̀-ẹ̀rọ olówó rẹpẹtẹ tí ó sọpé òun leè yanjú awọn ìyọnu kọ̀m̀pútà ti orilẹ-ede Britain: aláàrékérekè Jason Volta, tí Jake Lacy ṣe.
rows.output: The Ewe, the leader of the Igbimọ Ijọba, is a symbol of the complex and intricate nature of the British Empire's computer systems. Jason Volta, the brilliant scientist, and Jake Lacy, the skilled engineer, are two of the key figures in the development of these systems.
rows.reference: Meanwhile, the prime minister is falling dangerously under the spell of the charismatic tech billionaire who claims he can solve Britain's computer woes: the sinister Jason Volta, played by Jake Lacy.

rows.source: English ati Bough bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìrìn-àjò gígùn ti àwàdà aláriwo kan: wọ́n múra bíi àwọn agbáwo, wọn fi iná sí ilé oúnjẹ tójọjú ilẹ̀ Faranse kan; wọ́n ṣẹ̀dá ìdàrúdàpọ̀ nìbití wọ́n ti ṣe fàyàwọ́ ara wọn wọnú ọkọ̀ oju-omi ọlọ́lá ti Volta; ti English sì ṣe okùnfà aáwọ̀ bí ó ti ńgbìyànjú láti lo agbékọ́rí láti fi ara rẹ̀ mọ inu ilé ti Volta náà.
rows.output: The English and the French were both eager to stake their claim to a piece of the African continent: the English were as eager as the French to stake their claim to a piece of the African continent.
rows.reference: English and Bough begin their odyssey of farcical high-jinks: disguised as waiters, they set fire to a flash French restaurant; they create mayhem smuggling themselves aboard Volta's luxury yacht; and English triggers pure anarchy as he attempts to use a Virtual Reality headset to familiarise himself with the interior of Volta's house.

rows.source: Gbogbo àwọn ibi ìdúró níwọ́n fàyọ pẹ̀lú ìdanílójú fún àtẹ̀lé tógbẹ̀yín yẹn, ṣùgbọ́n bí ó ti jẹ́ eyiti ó fanimọ́ra àti aláriwo aláìkóraẹni-níìjánu tó yẹn, àwọn ohun díẹ̀ ninu TV àwọn ọmọdé wà nípa gbogbo nǹkan náà.
rows.output: All the bus stops are covered with advertisements, which are very annoying, especially when they are so close to the school, and the children are forced to look at them.
rows.reference: All the stops are certainly pulled out for that last sequence, but as amiable and boisterous as it is, there's quite a bit of kids' TV about the whole thing.

rows.source: Nǹkan alábọ́de tórẹwà.
rows.output: The most important thing is to be happy.
rows.reference: Pretty moderate stuff.

rows.source: ̀Àtipé bí ó ti rí pẹ̀lú àwọn sinnimá Johnny English N kò leè ran ara mi lọ́wó àfi kí ńronú: ṣe ilé iṣẹ́ sinnimá ilẹ́ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì náà kò leè fún Rowan Atkinson ni ipa kan eyiti yóò ṣe ìdájọ́ tòótọ́ sí tálẹ́ǹtì rẹ̀ ni?
rows.output: It's interesting to see how the Johnny English series has evolved over the years. I'm not sure if I'm ready to give up my own brand of humor, but I'm willing to try something new.
rows.reference: And as with the other Johnny English films I couldn't help thinking: can't the British film industry give Rowan Atkinson a role that really does justice to his talent?

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour ṣẹ wipé àwọn ti ńdọ́gbọ́n ètò kan fun àwọn ọmọ ilẹ̀ Britain láti ṣe iṣẹ́ ọjọ́ mẹ́rin lọ́sẹ̵̀ ṣùgbọn kí wọ́n san owó ọjọ́ máàrún fún wọn
rows.output: The Labour Party claims that there is a plan for British children to work four hours a day and pay them a weekly wage of one shilling.
rows.reference: Labour denies it is devising a plan for Britons to work a four day week but be paid for five days

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour ti Jeremy Corbyn fẹ́ lati ronú nípa ètò tóyàtọ̀ pátápátá kan eyiti yóò rísì kí àwọn ọmọ ilẹ̀ Britain máaṣe iṣẹ́ ọjọ́ mẹ́rin lọ́sẹ̵̀ - ṣùgbọn kí wọ́n gba owó fún ọjọ́ máàrún.
rows.output: The Labour Party, led by Jeremy Corbyn, is considering a proposal that would see workers in Britain receive a four-day working week, with a pay cut.
rows.reference: Jeremy Corbyn's Labour Party is to consider a radical plan which will see Britons working a four day week - but getting paid for five.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ náà ni wọn ròyin pé ó fẹ̵ àwọn olórí ilé iṣẹ́ láti fí àwọn ìfowópamọ́ tí wọ́n ṣe nípaṣẹ̀ ìyípadà ọpọlọ àtọwọ́dá sí àwọn òṣìṣẹ̵̵́ nípa fífún wọn ní àfikún ọjọ́ kan láti sinmi.
rows.output: The group was told that they would be given a chance to rest and recover from the long and tiring journey.
rows.reference: The party reportedly wants company bosses to pass on savings made through the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution to workers by giving them an extra day off.

rows.source: Yóò ríi pé àwọn òṣiṣẹ́ gbádùn òpin ọ̀sẹ̀ ọlọ́jọ́-mẹ́ta kan - ṣùgbọ́n wọ́n yóò mú iye owó náà lọ ilé síbẹ̀.
rows.output: You will find that the workers are paid a certain amount - they will not be paid any more than that.
rows.reference: It would see employees enjoy a three-day weekend - but still take home the same pay.

rows.source: Àwọn orísún sọpé èròǹgbà náà 'ṣe déédé' pẹ̀lú  ètò ọ̀rọ̀-ajé ti ẹgbẹ́ náà àti àwọn àgbékalẹ̀ láti dẹ̀gbẹ́ orilẹ-ede náà fún ojú rere àwọn òṣìṣẹ́.
rows.output: The leaders of the opposition parties supported the government's economic program and the budget of the national assembly with the hope of improving the country's image and attracting foreign investment.
rows.reference: Sources said the idea would 'fit' with the party's economic agenda and plans to tilt the country in favour of workers.

rows.source: Sísún sí ọ̀sẹ̀ ọlọ́jọ́-mẹ́rin kan ni Ìgbìmọ̀ Ẹgbẹ́ Àwọn Òṣìṣẹ́ ti fọwọsí bí ọ̀nà kan láti ṣàmúlò àǹfààní ti ọrọ̀-ajé tó ńyípadà náà.
rows.output: The 2018 EY World Entrepreneur of the Year award was presented to a 33-year-old founder of a company that has revolutionized the fashion industry.
rows.reference: Shifting to a four-day week has been endorsed by the Trades Union Congress as a way for workers to take advantage of the changing economy.

rows.source: Orísun ọ̀gá Ẹgbẹ̵̇́ Òṣèlú Labour kan sọ fún Sunday Times:  'Àtúgbéyẹ̀wò ìlàna ètò kan ni a ńreti láti kéde saájú òpin ọdún náà.
rows.output: The leader of the opposition Labour Party, Mr. Jeremy Corbyn, told the Sunday Times: 'We expect to be able to announce a deal by the end of the year.
rows.reference: A senior Labour Party source told The Sunday Times: 'A policy review is expected to be announced before the end of the year.

rows.source: 'Kòní ṣẹ́lẹ̀ ni òòru ọjọ́ kan ṣùgbọ́n ọ̀sẹ̀ iṣẹ́-ṣíṣe ọlọ́jọ́-mẹ́rin jẹ ìmísí kan eyiti ó ṣe déédéé wọnú ìgbéṣẹ̀ ẹgbẹ́ náà láti túnṣe ìmúdúró ọrọ̀-ajé náà fún ṣíṣe ojú rere sí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ àti bíi ọgbọn-àtiṣe ìdáṣẹ́sílẹ̀ ti ẹgbẹ́ náà.
rows.output: The government is not interested in the fact that there is a flood of imports, which is a result of the government's own policies, and it is not interested in the fact that there is a lack of production in the country.
rows.reference: 'It won't happen overnight but a four-day working week is an aspiration that fits in with the party's approach to rebalancing the economy in favour of the worker as well as the party's overall industrial strategy.'

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ Òṣèlú Labour kòní jẹ̵̵́ aláàkọ́kọ́ láti fọwosí irú èròǹgbà bẹ́ẹ̀, pẹ̀lú Ẹgbẹ́ Òṣèlú Green tó ńṣe ìléri ọ̀sẹ̀ iṣẹ́-ṣíṣe ọlọ́jọ́-mẹ́rin kan nígbà ìpolongo ìdìbò gbogbogbòò lọ́dún 2017.
rows.output: The Labour Party has not yet decided whether to support the Green Party, which has a candidate in the upcoming general elections in 2017.
rows.reference: The Labour Party would not be the first to endorse such an idea, with the Green Party pledging a four-day working week during its 2017 general election campaign.

rows.source: Ìlépa náà ni gbogbo Ẹgbẹ́ Òṣèlú Labour kò tíì fọwọsí bíi odidi kan lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́, botiwukori.
rows.output: The Labour Party has not yet been able to present a candidate for the election.
rows.reference: The aspiration is currently not being endorsed by the Labour Party as a whole, however.

rows.source: Agbẹnusọ Ẹgbẹ́ Òṣèlú Labour kan sọpé: 'Ọ̀sẹ̀ iṣẹ́-ṣíṣe ọlọ́jọ́-mẹ́rin kan kìí ṣe ìlànà ètò ẹgbẹ́ àtipé kì i ṣe ohun tí ẹgbẹ́ náà ńronú lé lórí.'
rows.output: The Labour Party's candidate for the governorship of Lagos State, Mr.ayo Opeyemi, said: 'The election is a four-year contract for the people of Lagos State, not for the party.
rows.reference: A Labour Party spokesman said: 'A four-day working week is not party policy and it is not being considered by the party.'

rows.source: Olórí Ìjọba Alátakò John McDonnell lo àpérò ti ọ̀sẹ̀ tókọjá ti Ẹgbẹ Òṣèlú Labour láti gbé ìran rẹ̀ fún àyipadà ti òṣèlu ọwọ-òsì ninu ọrọ̀-ajé náà jade.
rows.output: Leader of the Opposition John McDonnell used the opportunity to outline his vision for a change in the economic model of capitalism.
rows.reference: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used last week's Labour conference to flesh out his vision for a socialist revolution in the economy.

rows.source: Ọ̀gbẹ́ni McDonnell sọpé òun ti pinnu làti fi èékánná gba agbára padà kuro lọ́wọ́ 'àwọn olùdari tíwọn kò lójú' àti àwọn 'àwọn tó ńkórè' ninu àwọn ilé isẹ́ tó ńpèsè ohun ìgbáyé-gbádùn.
rows.output: Mr. McDonnell said he had decided to take the helm of the company, which had been criticized for its "lack of leadership" and "disarray" in the industry.
rows.reference: Mr McDonnell said he was determined to claw back power from 'faceless directors' and 'profiteers' at utility firms.

rows.source: Àwọn ètò olóri ìjọba alátako náà túmọ̀ sí wipe àwọn oníìpín ìdókòòwò lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ ní àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ omi-ẹ̀rọ leè má gba gbogbo ìpín wọn padà nitoripe ìjọba ẹgbẹ́ òṣ̵èlú Labour kan leè ṣe 'awọn àyọkúrò' lori àwọn ìdí ti ìwàkiwà ti wọn lérò.
rows.output: The ruling party's policies have led to the privatization of water resources, which has resulted in the return of water to the private sector because the Labour Party government is seen as 'pro-private' on the issue of water privatization.
rows.reference: The shadow chancellor's plans also mean current shareholders in water companies may not get back their entire stake as a Labour government could make 'deductions' on the grounds of perceived wrongdoing.

rows.source: Ó tún fi ìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀ nípa àwọn ètò láti fi àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ sínú àwọn ìgbìmọ aláṣẹ ilé iṣẹ̵́ àti láti ṣẹ̀dá Àwọn Owó Alájọni ti Oníǹkan lati máa fi ìdá mẹ́wàá ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún àwọn ìpìn ìdóòkòwò ti àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ aláàdáni fún àwọn abániṣiṣẹ́, ti wọn duro láti da àwọn èrè ìpìn ìdóòkòwò tí ó tó ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀ta pọ́ùn sápo.
rows.output: He also used his position to promote the idea of a Central Bank and to create the Central Bank of Nigeria to manage the money supply and to control the banking system, which was then used to control the economy, which was based on the gold standard.
rows.reference: He also confirmed plans to put workers on company boards and create Inclusive Ownership Funds to hand 10 per cent of private-sector firms' equity to employees, who stand to pocket annual dividends of up to £500.

rows.source: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy sọ ''Ọgọ́ta Ìṣẹ́jú'' bóyá ìwáàdí ti FBI nípa Kavanaugh leè yí ọkan wọn padà
rows.output: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy said "I think the FBI investigation of Kavanaugh was a whitewash"
rows.reference: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy tell "60 Minutes" whether the FBI's investigation of Kavanaugh could change their minds

rows.source: Ìwáàdí FBI náà sínú àwọn ẹ̀sùn tíwọ́n fi kan Adájọ́ Brett Kavanaugh ti dá ìdìbò tógbẹ̀yìn lórí ìfàkalẹ rẹ̀ fún iṣẹ́ Ilé Ẹjọ́ Tógajùlọ duro fún ó kéré tán ọ̀sẹ̀ kan, tí ó sì ńgbé ìbéèrè náà lori boya àwọn ohun ti àjọ náà rí leè sún èyíkéyìí àwọn aṣojú-ṣòfin àgbà ti ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Republican láti fa àtìlẹyìn kuro.
rows.output: The FBI's investigation into the allegations against Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh was limited to a background check, which is required for all Supreme Court nominees, and did not include any investigation into the claims of sexual misconduct. The investigation was conducted by the FBI's Office of Professional Responsibility, and the findings were not made public.
rows.reference: The FBI investigation into accusations against Judge Brett Kavanaugh has delayed a final vote on his nomination to the Supreme Court by at least a week, and raises the question of whether the bureau's findings could sway any Republican senators into pulling their support.

rows.source: Ninu ìfọ̀rọ̀wánilẹnuwò kan tó ńbọ́ sórí afẹ́fẹ́ lọ́jọ́ Àìkú, akọ̀ròyìn ''Ọgọ́ta Ìṣẹ́jú Scott Pelley béèrè lọ́wọ́ Àwọn Aṣojú-ṣòfin Àgbà John Kennedy àti Lindsey Graham bóyá FBI náà leè tú àṣírí ohunkóhun eyiti yóò darí wọn láti yí àwọn ọ̀kan wọn padà.
rows.output: In a recent interview with Scott Pelley, Senator Lindsey Graham and John Kennedy asked if the FBI had any evidence that would lead them to change their opinion of the candidates.
rows.reference: In an interview airing Sunday, "60 Minutes" correspondent Scott Pelley asked Republicans Sens. John Kennedy and Lindsey Graham whether the FBI could unearth anything that would lead them to change their minds.

rows.source: Kennedy farahàn bí ẹnití ó ńkó àkóyawọ́ ju akẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀ lati Gúúsù Carolina lọ.
rows.output: Kennedy was more liberal than most of his contemporaries in South Carolina.
rows.reference: Kennedy appeared more open than his colleague from South Carolina.

rows.source: ''Mo fẹ́ sọ, bí a tì ńretí,'' ni Kennedy sọ.
rows.output: "I want to say, as we expected," said Kennedy.
rows.reference: "I mean, of course," said Kennedy.

rows.source: ''Mo sọpé lílọ síbi ìgbẹ́jọ́ náà, mo sọ, mo ti bá adájọ́ Kavanaugh sọ̀rọ̀.
rows.output: "I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through this, I'm so sorry
rows.reference: "I said going into the hearing, I said, I've talked to Judge Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Mo pè é lẹ́yìn tí èyí ṣẹlẹ̀, tí ẹ̀sùn náà jáde, sọpé 'Ǹjẹ́ ó ṣe é?'
rows.output: I call you to witness that this deed is not done, that this evil is not wrought, so that you may say, 'Is it not done?'
rows.reference: I called him after this happened, that allegation came out, said, 'Did you do it?'

rows.source: Ó jẹ́ ẹnití ó ṣọkàn gíri, tóti pinnu, láìsiyèméji.''
rows.output: He who is wise, let him be wise.
rows.reference: He was resolute, determined, unequivocal."

rows.source: Ìbò ti Graham, botiwukori, farahàn bí eyiti wọ́n ṣètò ninu òkúta.
rows.output: Graham's Ibo, a botiwukori, farahann bí eyi ti o wà ninu oòku.
rows.reference: Graham's vote, however, appears set in stone.

rows.source: ''Ọkàn mi ti pinnu nípa Brett Kavanaugj àtipe yóò gba ẹ̀sùn abúgbàmu kan,'' ni o sọ.

rows.source: Moscow ti ń tẹnumọ́ pé iṣẹ́ àkànṣè Nord Stream 2 tí ó dá lórí gbígbé páìpù agbépo-rìn tí ó jẹ́ bílíọ́ọ̀nù dọ́là mọ́kànlá yóò sọ páìpù agbépo-rìn rẹ̀ di ìlọ́po méjì sí nǹkan bíi mítà kúbíìkì ọgọ́rùn-ún ó lé mẹ́wàá wáyé látàríi èròngbà wọn láti ní ìlọsíwájú nípa ètò ọrọ̀ ajé.

rows.output: The news has become a step forward for the world, a step forward for the heavens for those who witnessed the event.
rows.reference: For survivors, the situation was increasingly dire.

rows.source: “Ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí múnilára gidi gan” ni ohun tí ọmọ ọdún márùndínlógójì tí ó jẹ́ ìyá Risa Kusuma sọ bí ó ṣe ń tu ọmọ rẹ̀ tí wọ́n ń ṣàìsàn nínú ní àyè ìgbénìyàn sí ní ìlú Palu.
rows.output: "This incident is very sad" is what a 46-year-old mother, Risa Kusuma, said as she was releasing her sick child into the public space in the city of Palu.
rows.reference: "It feels very tense," said 35-year-old mother Risa Kusuma, comforting her feverish baby boy at an evacuation centre in the gutted city of Palu.

rows.source: "Ìṣẹ́jú-ìṣẹ́jú ni ọkọ̀ aláísàn máa ń gbé okú wọlé..
rows.output: "Each minute, the ambulance driver brings in a corpse."
rows.reference: "Every minute an ambulance brings in bodies.

rows.source: Omi tó mọ́ ṣọ̀wọ́n."
rows.output: The water is crystal clear.
rows.reference: Clean water is scarce."

rows.source: A rí àwọn olùgbé tó ń padà lọ sí ilé wọn tó ti bàjẹ́ láti mú ohun tí wọ́n bá lè rí mú nínú ẹrù wọn.
rows.output: We saw the residents returning to their homes that had been destroyed to pick up whatever they could find in their luggage.
rows.reference: Residents were seen returning to their destroyed homes, picking through waterlogged belongings, trying to salvage anything they could find.

rows.source: Ọ̀gọ̀ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn ló farapa nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ilẹ̀ mímì tí agbára rẹ̀ tó 7.5
rows.output: At least 7,500 people were injured in the earthquake.
rows.reference: Hundreds of people were injured and hospitals, damaged by the magnitude 7.5 quake, were overwhelmed.

rows.source: Díẹ̀ nínú àwọn tó fara káṣá nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí, èyí tí Dwi Harris tí ó ṣìṣe léjìká ,tí egun ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ sì kán sinmi ní iwájú ilé ìwòsàn Palu's Army, níbi tí àwọn aláìsàn ti ń rí ìtọ́jú gbà.
rows.output: Some of the first to be affected by this incident, which Dwi Harris, who was still active, and his injured leg were resting in front of Palu's Army Hospital, where patients were receiving treatment.
rows.reference: Some of the injured, including Dwi Haris, who suffered a broken back and shoulder, rested outside Palu's Army Hospital, where patients were being treated outdoors due to continuing strong aftershocks.

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú omijé ni Dwi fi ń ròyìn ìṣẹ̀lẹ ilẹ̀ mímì tí ó ká òun, ọmọbìnrin àti iyawo re mọ́ àjà-ile karùn-ún ní hòtẹ́ẹ̀lì.
rows.output: With tears, Dwi recounted the earthquake that had struck him, his daughter, and his wife, destroying their home in a hotel.
rows.reference: Tears filled his eyes as he recounted feeling the violent earthquake shake the fifth-floor hotel room he shared with his wife and daughter.

rows.source: A ò ráyè kankan láti sá àsálà fún ẹ̀mí wa.
rows.output: We have no right to run away from our destiny.
rows.reference: "There was no time to save ourselves.

rows.source: “Láàrin ògiri tó ti wó ni mo rún mọ́” Harris sọ fún Associated Press, ó tún ṣàfikún pé ayẹyẹ ìgbéyàwó kan ló gbé òun àti ẹbí òun wá sí ìlú Palu.
rows.output: "Between the walls that have collapsed, I ran to them," Harris told Associated Press, adding that a wedding party had brought him and his family to the city of Palu.
rows.reference: I was squeezed into the ruins of the wall, I think," Haris told Associated Press, adding that his family was in town for a wedding.

rows.source: “Mo kọ́kọ́ gbọ́ igbe ìyàwó mi nígbà tí ó ń kígbé fún ìrànlọ́wọ́, kí ó tó dákẹ́.
rows.output: I first heard my wife's screams when she was calling for help, before she was silenced.
rows.reference: "I heard my wife cry for help, but then silence.

rows.source: Mí ò mọ ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ sí ìyàwó àti ọmọ mi
rows.output: I don't know what happened to my wife and child.
rows.reference: I don't know what happened to her and my child.

rows.source: Mo ní ìrètí pé kò sí ohunkóhun tó ṣe wọ́n”
rows.output: I hope that nothing can stop them.
rows.reference: I hope they are safe."

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba US ní orílẹ̀èdè China fẹ̀sùn kan orílẹ̀èdè náà pé ó ń ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn orílẹ̀èdè mìíràn pẹ̀lú pípolówó ẹ̀tàn.
rows.output: The US ambassador to China accused the country of harming other nations with its fake news.
rows.reference: U.S. ambassador accuses China of 'bullying' with 'propaganda ads'

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn ọ̀sẹ̀ kan tí ìwé ìròyìn fún ìjọba China gbé ìròyìn olójúùwé mẹ́rin kan jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn kan ní US. Ìròyìn náà ṣe àtòólẹ̀ àǹfààní tó wà láàrin òwò láàrin China àti US, èyí tí aṣojú ìjọba náà na ìka àbùkù kan China pé ó ń fi àwọn ìwé ìròyìn orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà tan àwọn ènìyàn.
rows.output: After a week of newspaper coverage, the Chinese government's official newspaper published an article in the US that highlighted the benefits of trade between China and the US, which the Chinese government criticized as a way of promoting American newspapers.
rows.reference: A week after an official Chinese newspaper ran a four-page ad in a U.S. daily touting the mutual benefits of U.S.-China trade, the U.S. ambassador to China accused Beijing of using the American press to spread propaganda.

rows.source: U.S. Ààrẹ orílẹ̀èdè U.S. Donald Trump ní Ọjọ́rú tó kọjá tọ́ka sí ìròyìn tí China gbé jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register- ilé-iṣẹ́ ìwé ìròyìn tí ń tà jùlọ ní ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa fẹ̀sùn kan China pé ó ń gbìyànjú láti dásí ètò ìdìbò ilé fún ilé amòfin tí yóò wáyé ní ọjọ́ kẹfà oṣù kọọkànlá. Orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ pé àwọn kò mọwọ́-mẹsẹ̀ nípa ẹ̀sùn náà.
rows.output: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday accused China of trying to influence the upcoming Iowa caucuses, which are scheduled for February 3. The Chinese government has denied the allegations.
rows.reference: U.S. President Donald Trump last Wednesday referred to the China Daily's paid supplement in the Des Moines Register - the state of Iowa's biggest selling newspaper - after accusing China of seeking to meddle in the Nov. 6 U.S. congressional elections, a charge China denies.

rows.source: Ibu ẹnu atẹlu Trump ti Beijing n gbiyanju lati dasi ninu idibo U.S saami si ohun ti awọn osisẹ U.S sọ fun Reuters jẹ ipele tuntun ninu irusoke ipolongo ibo lọdọ Washington lati funmọ China.
rows.output: Trump's trade war with Beijing is trying to disrupt the U.S. election, according to something that U.S. officials told Reuters is a new level of campaign interference from China.
rows.reference: Trump's accusation that Beijing was trying to meddle in U.S. elections marked what U.S. officials told Reuters was a new phase in an escalating campaign by Washington to put pressure on China.

rows.source: Bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ kìí ṣe ohun àràmọ̀ndà kí àwọn ìjọba òkèèrè ṣe ìpolówó fún ìlọsíwájú ọrọ̀ ajé, rògbòdìyàn nípa ọrọ̀ ajé wà láàrin Beijing ati Washington, èyí tí ó sì fà á kí àwọn méjèèjì gbé owó lórí àwọn ọjà tí ó ń wọlé láti orílẹ̀èdè kejì.
rows.output: While it is not a trade war, the economic rivalry between Beijing and Washington has led both sides to impose tariffs on imports from the other country.
rows.reference: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.

rows.source: Àwọn onímọ̀ lórílèedè U.S. wòye pé China ṣe àfikún owó lè ọjà tó ń wọlé sí U.S. láti orílẹ̀èdè China pàápàá jùlọ ní àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ bíi Iowa tí ó gbárùkù Trump àti ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú rẹ̀.
rows.output: U.S. officials believe that China is adding to the trade surplus with the U.S. particularly in states like Iowa that are crucial to Trump and his political base.
rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba U.S. ni China àti Gómìnà tẹ́lẹ̀ rí fún ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa, ẹni tí ó ń ta ohun ògbìn sí China jù, Terry Branstad sọ pé China ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn òṣìṣẹ́, okoòwò àti àgbẹ̀ nílẹ̀ Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: The U.S. Ambassador to China and former Governor of Iowa, who has done more business with China than anyone, Terry Branstad, said that China has harmed American workers, businesses and farmers.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: Branstad wòye nínú ìwé tí ó kọ sínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register ní ọjọ́ Àìkú pé China ti sa gbogbo ipa wọn láti ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn nínú àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn ní Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: Branstad wrote in an op-ed published in the Des Moines Register on Sunday that China has taken a "very active role" in promoting disinformation in American media.
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: "Ìjọba China ń ṣe àmúlò ètò ìròyìn tí kò ní ìpalára láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba tí ó wà ní Amẹ́ríkà láti sanwó ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn àti irọ́ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register,” ni ohun tí Branstad kọ.
rows.output: "The Chinese government is using a propaganda system that is not transparent from the American government to subsidize the spread of lies and falsehoods in the Des Moines Register newspaper," wrote Branstad.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: "Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú pé “Lódì kejì ẹ̀wẹ̀, kò fi bẹ́ẹ̀ sí àwọn alátakò tàbí ààfihàn èrò àwọn ará China lórí irúfẹ́ ọwọ́ ti ìjọba fi mú ètò ọrọ̀ ajé. Èyí rí bẹ́ẹ̀ nítorí abẹ́ ìṣàkóso ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Chinese Communist Party ni àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn wà.
rows.output: "It also continued to say that "The second wave of the epidemic, did not have any effect on the opposition or the views of the Chinese people on the type of economic management that the government adopted. This was because under the control of the Chinese Communist Party, the media outlets were.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ó tún fikún un pé ọ̀kan nínú àwọn ògbóntarìgì ilé ìwé ìròyìn ní orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ láti tẹ iṣẹ́ òun sínú ìwé ìròyìn wọn bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé Branstad kò dárúkọ ìwé ìròyìn náà ní pàtó.
rows.output: He also added that one of the editors of a Chinese newspaper published an article about his work, even though Branstad was not named in the article.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ Ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì ń ya àwọn obìnrin kúrò pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ Kavanaugh, Àwọn Onímọ̀ kìlọ̀
rows.output: The Republican Party is splitting over the issue of Kavanaugh, Women's March warns
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú bí ọ̀pọ̀ nínú àwọn àgbà ọ̀jẹ̀ olóṣèlú ẹgbẹ́ republican ṣe ń gbárùkù ẹni tí wọ́n yàn ní ilé ẹjọ́ tí ó ga jù lọ pẹ̀lú gbogbo àwọn ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀, àwọn onímọ̀ tí ń kìlọ̀ pé ọ̀rọ̀ yìí yóò lẹ́yìn pàápàá jùlọ láti ọwọ́ àwọn obìnrin nínú ètò ìdìbò áàrin táàmù.
rows.output: With many of the leading Republican candidates for president now under indictment, some legal experts are warning that this trend is especially troubling for women in the party.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ náà ti fa ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀pọ̀ rúkèrúdò, àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sì ń takú àwọn yóò tún dìbò fún àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ wọn.
rows.output: The issue has caused a great deal of controversy, and Republican lawmakers are pressuring their colleagues to vote again for their candidates.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Ọ̀jọ̀gbọ́n nínú ẹ̀kọ́ ìṣèlú ní Maxwell School tí ó wà ní Yunifásítì Syracuse Grant Reheer ṣọ fún àwọn ìwé ìròyìn The Hill lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta pé ọ̀rọ̀ náà yóò lẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Professor of political science at the Maxwell School at Syracuse University Grant Reeher told the news outlet The Hill on Monday that the matter would follow.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reheer sọ pé òun kò rò bóyá ìgbésẹ̀ tí Amòfin Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) nípa pípè àjọ FBI láti wá ṣe ìwádìí àwọn ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanaugh yóò tó láti pẹ̀tù sọ́kàn àwọn olùdìbò tí inú ń bí lọ́wọ́ lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
rows.output: Reheer said he did not think that the action of Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) in calling the FBI to investigate the allegations against Kavanaugh would be enough to sway the voters who were already leaning on the issue.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: "“Àwọn obìnrin ò ní gbàgbé ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní àná, wọn kò ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ lónìí, wọn kò sì ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ nínú ètò ìdìbò tí yóò wáyé ní oṣù kọọkànlá” ni ohun tí Karine Jean-Pierre, olùbádámọ̀ràn àgbà àti agbẹnusọ gbogbo fún ẹgbẹ́ MoveOn sọ lọ́jọ Ẹtì, èyí tí ó sì jẹyọ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday, they will not forget it today, and they will not forget it in the election that will take place in November" said Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, on Thursday, as reported in the Washington, D.C.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: Oṣù kọọkànlá ń bọ̀! Ní ohun tí àwọn afẹ̀hónúhàn ń ké bí wọ́n ṣe fi ìtaara wọn hàn ní ilé Aṣòfin pẹ̀lú bí àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì tí ó wà ní ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń ṣàkóso ọ̀rọ̀ ilé ẹjọ́ ṣe ń tẹ̀síwájú láti yan Kavanaugh sípò. The Mic jẹ́ kí ó yé wa pé èyí wáyé lẹ́yìn ẹ̀rí dọ́kítà Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic ní ó ń jọ́bọ̀ ìròyìn.
rows.output: November is coming! The Mic is here to tell us that this is happening after the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, the Mic is here to tell us that she is a doctor.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: Onímọ̀ ìṣèlú Stu Rothenberg sọ “Ìmọ̀sílára kò ní í sí lára àwọn ènìyàn, èyí yóò sì mú wọn dìbò”
rows.output: Political analyst Stu Rothenberg said "The mood is not in the people, this will lead them to vote"
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: Àwọn ènìyàn tilẹ̀ ti ń sọ pé àwọn kò lè dúró kí ọjọ́ ìdìbò dé.
rows.output: Some people have even said they can't wait for the election day.
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Ó ṣeéṣe kí ìmọ̀sílára pọ̀ sí pàápàá jùlọ láàrin àwọn obìnrin tí ó wà ní ìgbèríko àti àwọn ọmọbìnrin láàrin ọmọ ọdún méjìdínlógún sí óòkandínlọ́gbọ̀n tí wọ́n ò nífẹ̀ẹ́ ààrẹ, síbẹ̀ tí wọ́n kìí dìbò.”
rows.output: It is possible that the sense of entitlement is particularly strong among women in the informal sector and among young women aged 18 to 29 who do not support the president, but do vote.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Kí Ford tó jẹ́rìí ní gbangba nípa ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀ tí ó fi kan Kavanaugh ni àwọn onímọ̀ ti ń kìlọ̀ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí yíyan Kavanaugh sípò bu ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì lọ́wọ́.
rows.output: Before Ford confirmed her allegations of sexual assault against Kavanaugh, there were warnings from experts that it was possible that the nomination of Kavanaugh would be a blow to the Republican Party.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí ti dá yánpọyánrin kalẹ̀ fún ẹgbẹ́ wa” ni ohun tí Michael Steele tí ó fìgbà kan jẹ́ alága fún ìgbìmọ̀ gbogbogbò ní ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sọ ní ọ̀sẹ̀ tó kọjá gẹ́gẹ́ bí NBC News ṣe sọ.
rows.output: "This phrase has been used to whip up a frenzy in our ranks" is what Michael Steele, a former chairman of the Republican National Committee, said last week, according to NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí kìí ṣe nípa bóyá àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì yan Kavanaugh sípò nìkan, ó tún nííṣe pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì fi mú ọ̀rọ̀ náà àti ọwọ́ tí wọ́n fi mú Ford” Olùdarí ẹgbẹ́ tó ń ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ fún ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Dẹ́mókírààtì Priorities USA, Guy Cecil ló sọ èyí fún ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn náà.
rows.output: "This is not just about whether Republican voters chose Kavanaugh, but also about the hand that Republican voters gave to the party and the hand that the party gave to Ford," said Guy Cecil, the manager of Priorities USA, a Democratic super PAC, in an interview with the news organization.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀, èrò àwọn ọmọ Amẹ́ríkà pín sí méjì lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà pẹ̀lú bí wọn kò mọ ẹni tí ó yẹ kí wọ́n gbàgbọ́ nínú Kavanaugh àti Ford.
rows.output: However, American public opinion is divided on the issue, with people unsure of who to believe in Kavanaugh and Ford.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Ìdìbò afèròhàn tí YouGov gbé kalẹ̀ fi hàn pé ìdá mọ́kànlelógoji nínú àwọn tó kópa nínú ètò ìdìbò náà sọ pé àwọn gba Ford gbọ́ nígbà tí ìdá márùndínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn gba Kavanaugh gbọ́.
rows.output: The YouGov poll found that 51% of respondents said they trust Ford, while 49% said they trust Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Ìdá méjìdínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Kavanaugh ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí rẹ̀ nígbà tí ìdá ọgbọ̀n ló gbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Ford ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí tirẹ̀ bákan náà.
rows.output: 48% believe that Kavanaugh lied under oath, while 30% believe that Ford lied under oath.

rows.source: Iṣẹ́ àkànṣe Ògbóǹtarìgì onímọ̀ ẹ̀rọ, Inrupt, jẹ́ ilé iṣẹ́ tí ó dúró lórí i orísun ìpìlẹ̀ iṣẹ́ Berners-Lee.
rows.output: The World Wide Web project, Inrupt, is a company based on the foundation's work by Berners-Lee.

rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.output: In an interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee said that the idea behind Inrupt was to "take over the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “A gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe báyìí," ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ nípa ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ náà.
rows.output: "We must do this now," he said of the beginning.

rows.source: "Ó jẹ́ àkókò onítàn."
rows.output: "It is a time of stories."

rows.output: The initiative uses Solid's technology to empower people to create their own "personal data stores online" or PODs.

rows.source: Ó le ní àwọn àtòkọ olùbásọ̀rọ̀, ohun-àti-ṣe, kàlẹ́ńdà, ibi ìpamọ́ orin àti àwọn irinṣẹ́ àdáni àti àfyṣiṣẹ́ mìràn.
rows.output: It can have contact lists, to-do lists, calendars, music storage, and other custom and automated tools.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ó dábí Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack àti Spotify tí gbogbo wọ́n wà nílẹ̀ lórí aṣawákiri ní àṣìkò kannáà.

rows.source: Ohun tí ó dá yàtọ̀ nípa ilé ìtàjà dátà àdáni ayelujára pé aṣàmúlò ló kù sí lọ́wọ́ láti mọ ẹni tí ó le ráyèsí àti irú ìwífún tó le ráyèsí.

rows.output: The company is called "Data-driven personalization."

rows.source: Èròńgbà fún Inrupt, gẹ́gẹ́bí Olùdásílẹ̀ ilé iṣẹ́ náà John Bruce ṣe sọ, ni pé ó wá fún ilé iṣẹ̀ láti mú àwọn ohun àmúlò, ìlànà àti àwọn ọgbọ́n àtinúdá láti ṣèrànwọ́ láti mú kí Solid wà nílẹ̀ fún gbogbo ènìyàn.
rows.output: The mission for Inrupt, as stated by the founder of the company John Bruce, is to bring the tools, processes, and methodologies to help make Solid real for everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ náà ní Berners-Lee, Bruce, ètò ìpèsè ààbò tí IBM rà, àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ fúngbàdíẹ̀ tí wọ́n gbà láti ṣiṣẹ́ lórí iṣẹ́ àkànṣe náà, àti àwùjọ àwọn akọkóòdù tí wọ́n jẹ́ olùfarajìn.
rows.output: The project was funded by IBM, and included Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security provision system that IBM had purchased, a few employees who were hired to work on the project, and a community of volunteers who were passionate about the project.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Bẹ́rẹ̀ láti ọ̀ṣẹ̀ yìí, àwọn aṣàmúàgbà ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ káàkiri àgbáyé le ṣldá àwọn ìṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ tiwọ́n ní àkàtà wọ́n nípa lílo àwọn irínṣẹ́ tó wà nílẹ̀ lórí wẹ́ẹ̀bù Inrupt.
rows.output: Starting this month, global tech giants can launch their own decentralized apps on the Inrupt network using tools available on the web.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee sọ pé òun àti àwọn akẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀ kò bá “Facebook àti Google” sọ̀rọ̀ nípa bóyá tàbí ki wọ́n ṣètò ìyípadà pátápátá níbi gbogbo àwòṣe òkòwò wọn tí máa yípadà tàbí kí ó soríkodò láìròtẹ́lẹ̀.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that he and his colleagues did not talk to "Facebook and Google" about whether or not to make a complete change in all their commercial models that would be irreversible.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: "Àwa kò bèèrè fún ìyànda wọn."
rows.output: "We don't need their mercy."

rows.source: Nínú àtljíṣẹ́ lórí Medium tí wọ́n tẹ̀jáde ní sátidé, Berners-Lee kọ lórí Inrupts pé “àfojúsùn ni láti pèsè ohun àmúṣagbara olókòwò àti àyíká ilegbèè láti ṣèrànwọ́ ìdáàbòbò àti àmúyẹ wẹ́ẹ̀bù tí a fi Solid ṣe.”
rows.output: In a Medium post published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that "the goal is to provide a free, open, and sustainable platform for the web that is built on Solid."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Ní 1994, Berners-Lee tí Ítánẹ̀ẹ̀tì padà nígbàtí ó dá ilé iṣẹ́ wẹ́ẹ̀bù ayélujára sílẹ̀ ní ilé ẹ̀kọ́ ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ ní Massachusetts.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee returned to the Internet when he founded the World Wide Web Consortium at the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at MIT.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: Ní àwọn oṣù bí díẹ̀ ṣẹ́yìn, Berners-Lee ni ó ti jẹ́ ẹní àwòkọ́ṣe níbi ìjíròrò aláìṣègbè.
rows.output: In the past few months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal critic in the debate over net neutrality.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Kódà lákòókò ìṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ Inrupt, Berners-Lee sì máa jẹ́ Olùdásílẹ̀ àti Olùdarí ilé iṣẹ́ wẹ́ẹ̀bù ayélujára, ìpìlẹ̀ Wẹ́ẹ̀bù àti ilé iṣẹ́ Dátà Àjọlò.
rows.output: Even during the launch of Inrupt, Berners-Lee would remain the Founder and Director of the World Wide Web Consortium, the foundation of the Web and the Internet Data Consortium.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: "Mó ní ìrétí ayọ lórí sáà tó ń bọ̀ yìí lórí wẹ́ẹ̀bù,” Bermers-Lee ṣàfikún ọ̀rọ̀.
rows.output: "I'm also very excited about the future of the web," Bermers-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.output: Bernard Vann: The Victoria Cross awarded to WW1 soldiers is celebrated

rows.reference: Germany's new warship postponed yet again

rows.source: Àkọ̀tun Ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi ti Jámáànù ní ó yẹ kí ó ti di fífi lọ́lẹ̀ ní ọdún 2014 láti pààrọ̀ àwọn ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi Sáà-ogún Dúkùú, ṣùgbọ́n kò ní rí bẹ́ẹ̀ títí di, ó kéré jù, ọdún í ó ń bọ̀ nítorí àwọn èròjà tó ti bàjẹ̀ àti àwọn ìnáwò tó ti ṣarajọ, ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn abẹ́léni ó jábọ̀ rẹ̀.
rows.output: The German Navy's Type 212A submarine was originally scheduled to be decommissioned in 2014 to make way for the Type 214 submarine, but this was not done until at least the next year due to technical problems and budget cuts, which the defense industry journal reported.
rows.reference: German Navy's newest frigate should have been commissioned in 2014 to replace ageing Cold War-era warships, but it won't be there until at least the next year due to faulty systems and snowballing cost, local media reported.

rows.source: Síṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ "Rheinland-Pfalz," olórí ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi tí ìsọ̀rí fírígéètì Baden-Wuerttemberg tuntun nini, ni ó ti di sísún ṣíwájú títi di ìdájì àkọ́kọ́ ọdún 2019, gẹ́gẹ́bi ìwé ìròyìn Die Zeit ṣe sọ tí ọgá ológun kan sọ.
rows.output: Launching "Rheinland-Pfalz," the new commander of the naval force of the Baden-Wuerttemberg state flag, has been ahead of schedule since the first quarter of 2019, as reported by the newspaper Die Zeit.
rows.reference: Commissioning of the "Rheinland-Pfalz," the lead ship of the brand new Baden-Wuerttemberg-class frigates, has now been postponed until the first half of 2019, according to Die Zeit newspaper citing a military spokesman.

rows.source: Ó yẹ kí ọkọ̀ ojú omi nlá náà darapọ̀ ní 2014, ṣùgbọ̀n àwọn wàhálà ìṣòro lẹ́yìn ìfakalẹ̀ rẹ̀ ní ó mú kí ìgbẹ́kẹ́lé nínú itẹ̀síwájú àkànṣe iṣẹ́ náà já sófo.
rows.output: The project was supposed to be completed in 2014, but the challenges that followed its suspension led to a loss of confidence in the project's progress.

rows.output: Four large ferries of the Baden-Wuerttemberg series, which were built for the German Navy, will come as substitutes for the Bremen class frigates from 2007.

rows.output: It will always be like that.
rows.reference: It's normal.

rows.source: Wọn fẹ di olokiki lati pe orukọ mi, ṣugbọn lara iṣẹ naa ni.
rows.output: They want to be known by my name, but within the work itself.
rows.reference: They want to be famous to say my name, but it is part of the job.

rows.source: Mo jẹ́ onídùn ọkùnrin tí gbogbo rẹ̀ sì dára, " agbábọ̀ọ̀lù náa sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, ó ń rẹ́rín múṣẹ́.
rows.output: I'm a good guy, all of it is good, the ball said, smiling.
rows.reference: I am a happy man and all good," the player added, smiling.

rows.source: Àwọn àmòfin Ronaldo ń gbaradì láti pe Der Spiegel lẹ́jọ́ lórí ìfẹ̀sùnkanni èké, tí wọ́n pè ní “Ìròyìn tí kò tọ́ nípa ìfurasíni ní agbègbè àdani ẹni”. Gẹ́gẹ́bí Reuters ṣe sọ.
rows.output: Ronaldo's lawyers are demanding that Der Spiegel retract the false report, which is called "False Reporting in the Private Sphere of a Person", according to Reuters.
rows.reference: Ronaldo's lawyers are preparing to sue Der Spiegel over the allegations, which they have called "an inadmissible reporting of suspicions in the area of privacy," according to Reuters.

rows.source: Amòfin Christian Schertz sọ pé agbábọ́ọ̀lù náà máa bèèrè fún ẹ̀tọ́ ìbanilórúkọjẹ́ fún “ìbanilórúkọjẹ́ ní ìwọ̀n tí ó lọ gẹ́gẹ́bí ìwúwosí ìrúfin náà, tí ó ṣeéṣe kí ó jẹ́ ọ̀kan pàtàkì jùlọ nínú ẹ̀tọ́ ọmọnìyàn láti bí ọdún díẹ́ ṣẹ́yìn."
rows.output: Attorney Christian Schertz said the ball would require a constitutional amendment for "the right to abortion in the same way that the right to life is recognized as a fundamental right of mankind, which has been recognized for decades."
rows.reference: Lawyer Christian Schertz said the player would seek compensation for "moral damages in an amount corresponding to the gravity of the infringement, which is probably one of the most serious violations of personal rights in recent years."

rows.source: Ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ìfẹ́sùnkanni náà ní wọ́n sọ pé ó wáyé ní ọṣù kẹfà 2009 ní Ilé ìtura Palms àt Casino ni Las Vegas.
rows.output: The incident of the kidnapping occurred in June 2009 at the Palms Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas.
rows.reference: The alleged incident is said to have taken place in June 2009 at a suite at the Palms Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas.

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n ti padé ní pátí alẹ́, Ronaldao àti Mayorga ní wọ́n jábọ̀ pé wọn padà sí yàrá agbábọ̀ọ̀lù náà., níbi tí wọn ti fé ẹ̀sùn tí kò tíì lẹ́rìí k[sn pé ó fi ìpa báá a lòpọ̀ láti fùrọ̀, gẹ́gẹ́bí àkọ̀sílẹ̀ ìwé tí wọ̀n kọ ní Ilé ẹjọ Agbègbe Clark ní́ Nevada.
rows.output: After meeting in the park, Ronaldao and Mayorga were arrested and charged with returning to the football field, where they were accused of having sex in public, as stated in the written record of the Clark County Court in Nevada.
rows.reference: After meeting in a nightclub, Ronaldo and Mayorga reportedly went back to the player's room, where he allegedly anally raped her, according to papers filed at Clark County District Court in Nevada.

rows.source: Mayorga sọ wípé Ronaldo wólẹ̀ níwájú òhun lẹ́yìn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà tí ó sì sọ fún òun pé “99 ìdá ọgọ́rùn ún” ní òun fi jẹ́ “ọkùrin rere” tí “ìdá kan l’ọ́gọ́rù ún” sì já òhun kulẹ̀.
rows.output: Mayorga said Ronaldo collapsed in front of him after the incident and told him he was "99 percent" a "good guy" and "one percent" was "bad."
rows.reference: Mayorga claims Ronaldo fell to his knees after the alleged incident and told her he was "99 percent" a "good guy" let down by the "one percent."

rows.source: Àwọn àkọsílẹ̀ fi yé wa pé Ronaldo fi ìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀ pé àwọn méjèèjì ní ìbálòpọ̀, ṣùgbọ́n àjọ̀mọ̀àwọn méjèèjì ní.
rows.output: The documents indicate that Ronaldo confirmed that both had a sexual relationship, but the couple deny it.
rows.reference: The documents claim that Ronaldo confirmed the pair had sex, but that it was consensual.

rows.source: Mayorga tún sọ bákan náà pé òun lọ sí t’ọlọ́pàá àtipé òun yà àwọn àwòrán ìpalára tí òun ní ní ìlé ìwòsàn kan, ṣùgbọ́n tí òwun gbà láti yanjú ọ̀rọ̀ náà lábẹ́lé nítorípé òwn “ẹ̀rù gbíga ẹ̀sàn bà á” àtí pé òun ní àibàlẹ̀ ọkàn nípa “ìdójútì káríáyé”
rows.output: Mayorga also said that he went to the police station and left pictures of his injuries from a hospital, but he agreed to settle the matter quietly because he was "scared of the consequences" and had a bad conscience about "the international scandal."
rows.reference: Mayorga also claims she went to the police and had photographs taken of her injuries at a hospital, but later agreed to an out-of-court settlement because she felt "terrified of retaliation" and was worried about "being publicly humiliated."

rows.source: ẹni ọgbọ̀n ọdún ó lé mẹ́rin náà sọ pé òun ṣẹṣẹ̀ ń wá bíòun ṣe máa yí ìpínnu náà padà ní nítorí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà ni ó ń jẹ́ ọgbẹ́ ọkàn fún òun.
rows.output: A 30-year-old man said he was recently trying to change his decision because of the event, which was a heartbreak for him.
rows.reference: The 34-year-old says she is now seeking to overturn the settlement as she continues to be traumatized by the alleged incident.

rows.source: Ronaldo ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ fẹ́ darapọ̀ mọ́ Real Madrid láti Manchester United ni àkókò ìkọlù náà, àtipé ní sọ́mà yìí ló lọ sí òmìràn ìtálí Juve nínú ìṣòwò €100.
rows.output: Ronaldo had just joined Real Madrid from Manchester United during the transfer window, and this was the first time he was facing another Italian team in the market.
rows.reference: Ronaldo was on the verge of joining Real Madrid from Manchester United at the time of the alleged assault, and this summer moved to Italian giants Juve in a €100 million deal.

rows.source: Brexit: UK ‘má kábámọ̀ títí ayé’ nípa pípàdńu àwọn àṣemọ́tò
rows.output: Brexit: UK 'will not apologize' for losing passport privileges
rows.reference: Brexit: UK 'would forever regret' losing carmakers

rows.source: Orílẹ̀ èdè UK "má kábámọ̀ títí ayé" tí ó bá sọ ipò rẹ̀ nù bíi olórí lágbàáyé nínú mọ́tò ṣiṣẹ́ lẹ́yìn Brexit, àkswé fún okòòwò Greg Clark ló sọ bẹ́ẹ.
rows.output: The UK government "will not apologize" for its position as a global leader in the automotive industry after Brexit, Trade Secretary Greg Clark said.
rows.reference: The UK "would regret it forever" if it lost its status as a world leader in car manufacturing after Brexit, Business Secretary Greg Clark has said.

rows.source: Ótún sọ síwájú pé “nípa” pé Toyota UK ti sọ fún BBC pé tí Bírítéénì bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láì ní àdéhùn ìsòwò tó só pọ̀, ó máa ṣe ìdádúró ìgbéjáde-iṣẹ̀ ní ilé iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Burnaston, ní ẹ̀bá Derby.
rows.output: The right-wing group said "in the event" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a trade deal, it would halt production at its Burnaston plant, near Derby.
rows.reference: He added it was "concerning" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal it would temporarily halt production at its factory in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: "A nílò àdéhùn ìṣòwò,” Ọ̀gbẹ́ni Clark ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need a trade agreement," Mr. Clark said.
rows.reference: "We need a deal," Mr Clark said.

rows.source: Aṣemọ́tò Jàpáàanù sọ pé ipa ààlà máa ṣe ìdádúró tí ó bá lọ jẹ́ pé kò sí àd’hpùn ìṣòwò Brexit lẹ́ mú kí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́ wà.
rows.output: The Japanese government says the impact of the border shutdown will be a significant blow to the economy, and that the loss of jobs will be a major factor in the UK's departure from the EU.
rows.reference: The Japanese carmaker said the impact of border delays in the event of a no-deal Brexit could cost jobs.

rows.source: Ẹ̀rọ̀ iṣẹ́ Burnaston - tí ó ń ṣe Toyota Auris àti Avensis - pèsè mọ́tò tó súnmọ́ 150,000 ní ọdún tó kọjá tí ó sì jẹ́ pé 90% ní wọ́n ṣàgbéjáde sí Ìṣọ̀kan Yúròpù tó kù.
rows.output: The Burnaston plant, which manufactures the Toyota Auris and Avensis, produced approximately 150,000 vehicles last year, with 90% of those exports going to the rest of Europe.
rows.reference: The Burnaston plant - which makes Toyota's Auris and Avensis - produced nearly 150,000 cars last year of which 90% were exported to the rest of the European Union.

rows.source: "Ìwòyé mi ni pé tí Bírítéènì ba fi le jáde kúrò ní EU láìròtẹ́lẹ̀ ní òpin oṣù kẹta, ìgbéjáde máa dúró ní ilé iṣẹ́ wa,” Marvi Cooke ni ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, Alákòóso adarí ní Burnaston.
rows.output: "My belief is that if Britain is able to leave the EU without a hitch by the end of March, then the exit will be smooth for our factory," said Marvi Cooke, managing director of Burnaston.
rows.reference: "My view is that if Britain crashes out of the EU at the end of March we will see production stops in our factory," said Marvin Cooke, Toyota's managing director at Burnaston.

rows.source: Àwọn aṣemọ́tò UK tí fi ìjayà wọn hàn nípa fífi EU sílẹ̀ láìní àdéhùn lórí bí kíkọjá láàlà òkòwò ṣe máa ṣiṣẹ́, gẹ́gẹ́bí i Honda, BMW àti Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.output: UK carmakers threaten to halt production if EU leaves without a deal on post-Brexit trade, as Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.reference: Other UK car manufacturers have raised fears about leaving the EU without agreement on how cross-border trade will function, including Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.

rows.source: BMW, fún àpẹẹrẹ, sọ pé ò máa ti Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ kékeré rẹ̀ ní Oxford fún oṣù kan tí ó tẹ̀lé Brexit.
rows.output: For example, BMW said it would not use its Mini plant in Oxford for a month after Brexit.
rows.reference: BMW, for example, says it will close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month following Brexit.

rows.source: Ohun ìkọminú jùlọ jẹ́mọ́ ohun tí àwọn aṣemọ́tò sọ pé ọ jẹ àwọń èwu ètò ìpèsè tí ó bá ṣẹlẹ̀ pé kò sí àdéhun ìṣòwò Brexit.
rows.output: The most significant thing is what the technocrats say that you are the risks of the supply chain that would occur if there is no post-Brexit trade agreement.
rows.reference: The main concerns relate to what carmakers say are supply chain risks in the event of a no-deal Brexit.

rows.source: Ìgbéjáde àtòpọ̀ Toyota dá lórí i “tó bá àkókò mu”, pẹ̀lú àwọn ẹ̀yà ara rẹ̀ tí ó ń wọlé ní gbogbo ìṣẹ́jú 37 láti ọ̀dọ̀ olùgbéjáde wọn ní UK àti EU fún àwọn mọ́tò láti tà jáde.
rows.output: The launch of Toyota's new model is based on "just-in-time", with its components arriving every 37 seconds from its production plants in the UK and EU for sale.
rows.reference: Toyota's production line is run on a "just-in-time" basis, with parts arriving every 37 minutes from suppliers in both the UK and the EU for cars made to order.

rows.source: Tí UK bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láìsí àdéhùn ìṣòwò ní 29 oṣù kẹta, ìdíwọ́ le wà ní ààlà ibode tí àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ sọ pé o le já sí ìdádúro àti àìnító àwọn ẹ̀yà ara.
rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a trade agreement on 29 March, there could be delays at the border, companies say, which could lead to shortages and price increases.
rows.reference: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on 29 March, there could be disruption at the border which the industry says could lead to delays and shortages of parts.

rows.source: Kò ní ṣeéṣe fún Tòyótà láti ní ọjà nílẹ̀ tó ju ìwọ̀n ọjọ́ kan lọ ní ibi Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Derbyshire, ilé iṣẹ́ náà ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, àtipé ìgbéṣẹ́jáde máa dáwọ́ dúró.
rows.output: It is impossible for Toyotas to have a market value of more than a day's work in Derbyshire, the company said, and production will be suspended.
rows.reference: It would be impossible for Toyota to hold more than a day's worth of inventory at its Derbyshire plant, the company said, and so production would be stopped.

rows.source: Mr Clark sọ pé ète Theresa May fún ìbáṣepọ̀ ọjọ́ iwájú pẹ̀lú EU jẹ́ “àmọ̀ǹmọ̀ṣe láti yàgò fún àwọn àyẹ́wò ní ààlà ìbodè náà.”
rows.output: Mr. Clark said that Theresa May's plan for future relations with the EU is "a recipe for avoiding scrutiny at the border."
rows.reference: Mr Clark said Theresa May's Chequers plan for future relations with the EU is "precisely calibrated to avoid those checks at the border."

rows.source: "A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò. A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò tó dára jùlọ tí ó máa gbà wá láàyè bí mo ṣe sọ, tí kò kì í ṣe àṣeyọrí nìkán ní àkókò yì tí a lé gbàdún, ṣùgbọ́n fún wa láti má le sọ àǹfààní yìí nù,” ó sọ fún ètò rédíò 4 BBC Lónìí bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need a trade agreement. We need a better trade agreement that will allow us to live as I say, not just a success in the time we are given, but to prevent us from missing out on this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today program.
rows.reference: "We need to have a deal. We want to have the best deal that will allow as I say not just the success at present to be enjoyed but for us to grasp this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

rows.source: "Ẹ̀rí àrídájú tí kìíṣe láti ọ̀dọ̀ Toyotà nìkan ṣùgbọ́n tí ó jẹ́ ti àwọn àṣemọ́tò jáde míràn ní pé a nílò láti rí dájú pé a tẹ̀síwájú nínú ohun tí a ti ńṣe láṣeyọrílórí àwọn ààtò ìpèsè.”
rows.output: "Unambiguous evidence from Toyota alone, but also from other manufacturers, is that we need to ensure that we continue to do what we have been doing in a responsible manner regarding procurement contracts."
rows.reference: "The evidence from not just Toyota but other manufacturers is that we need to absolutely be able to continue what has been a highly successful set of supply chains."

rows.source: Toyota kò le sọ pàtò bí ó ṣe máa pẹ́ tó kí ìgbéṣẹ́jáde tó le dáwọ́ dúró, ṣùgbọ́n nígbà tí ó bá ṣe díẹ̀, ó kìlọ̀ pé àwọn ìṣùnà mìràn tó le jẹyọ máa ṣàdínkù ìledíje ẹ̀rọ ìṣẹ́ tí ó sì máa jásí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́.
rows.output: Toyota cannot predict how long the production stoppage will last, but when it does, it warns that other factors may reduce the incentive for automakers to produce more and may lead to job losses.
rows.reference: Toyota was unable to say how long production would be stopped, but in the longer term, warned that added costs would reduce the plant's competitiveness and eventually cost jobs.

rows.source: Peter Tsouvallaris, tí ó ti ṣiṣẹ́ ní Burnaston fún ọdún 24 tí ó sì jẹ́ adárí ìpàdé ìgbìmọ̀ òkòwò níibi ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ náà, sọ pé ó kàn àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ òun gan an: "Ní ìrírí mi, ní kété tí àwọn iṣẹ́ yìí bá lọ, wọ̀n kó ní padà wá mọ́ láeláee.
rows.output: Peter Tsouvallaris, who had worked at Burnaston for 24 years and was the head of the economic committee at the plant, said that he had only been able to recruit a few members: "In my experience, as soon as these operations are closed, they immediately return to their homes.
rows.reference: Peter Tsouvallaris, who has worked at Burnaston for 24 years and is the Unite union convenor at the plant, said his members are increasingly concerned: "In my experience once these jobs go they never come back.

rows.source: Agbẹnusọ fún ìjọba kan sọ wípé: "A ti taari èròǹgbà tí ó ṣe gẹ́gẹ́ tí ó ṣì mú ọgbọ́n wa fún ọjọ́ iwájú ìbáṣepọ̀ wa pẹ̀lú EU.”
rows.output: The government spokesman said: "We have taken into account the concerns that have been expressed and we have maintained our negotiating position for our future relationship with the EU."
rows.reference: A government spokesperson said: "We have put forward a precise and credible plan for our future relationship with the EU."

rows.source: Ìpàdé Trump pẹ̀lú Rosenstein lé ní ìdádúró lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi, Ilé Funfun Báláu ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: Trump's meeting with Rosenstein was delayed again, the White House said.
rows.reference: Trump meeting with Rosenstein may be delayed again, says White House

rows.source: Ìpàdé onípinnu-ńlá Donald Trump pẹ̀lú ìgbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò Rod Rosenstein le “sún síwájú fún ọ̀ṣẹ̀ kan mìíràn” bí ìjà lórí ẹnítí wọn dábàá fún ilé ẹjọ́ gíga Brett kavanaugh ṣe tẹ́ ṣíwájú, Ilé Funfun Báláú ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ ní Ọjọ́ ìsinmi.
rows.output: A high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump and Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein could "telescope into another week" if the controversy over Trump's nominee for the Supreme Court, Brett Kavanaugh, continues, White House press secretary Sarah Sanders said on Sunday.
rows.reference: Donald Trump's high-stakes meeting with deputy attorney general Rod Rosenstein could be "pushed back another week" as the fight over supreme court nominee Brett Kavanaugh continues, the White House said on Sunday.

rows.source: Rosensteinní ó ń ṣàbójútó iṣẹ́ àgbẹjọ́rò pàtàkì Robert Mueller, tí ó ń ṣe ìwádìí lórí i ìkọlù Rọ́ṣíà lórí ìdìbò, ìbáṣepọ̀ láàrin àwọn òṣiṣẹ́ Trump àti Rọ́ṣíà àti bí ó ṣe ṣẹéṣe sí fún ààrẹ láti dènà ètò ìdájọ tó péye.
rows.output: Rosenstein is overseeing a special counsel, Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian interference in the election, the relationship between Trump's campaign and Russia, and the possibility of the president obstructing justice.
rows.reference: Rosenstein oversees the work of special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian election interference, links between Trump aides and Russia and potential obstruction of justice by the president.

rows.source: Bóyá Trump máa dá igbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò dúró tàbí kò ní ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, tí ó máa wá mú kí òmínira Mueller níra, ti jẹ́ kí Washington ṣòfófo fú ọ̀pọ̀ oṣù ṣẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Perhaps Trump will fire the special prosecutor or not, but he will certainly harass Mueller, and let Washington spin for months.
rows.reference: Whether or not Trump will fire the deputy attorney general, and thereby endanger Mueller's independence, has fuelled Washington gossip for months.

rows.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ oṣù yìí, ìwé ìròyìn New York Times jábọ̀ pé Rosenstein jíròrò lórí i pé oùn fẹ́ fí wáyà sára láti ṣe àkásílẹ̀ ìtàkurọ̀sọ pẹ̀lú Trump àti ìṣeéṣesí láti yọ ààrẹ nínú àtúnṣe 25.
rows.output: At the beginning of this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed the possibility of wearing a wire to record Trump and his associates in order to build a case to remove him from office under the 25th Amendment.
rows.reference: Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed wearing a wire to record conversations with Trump and the possibility of removing the president via the 25th amendment.

rows.source: Rosenstein ní ìròyìn yí kò rí bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: Rosenstein said the report did not find that.
rows.reference: Rosenstein denied the report.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n ní ọjọ́ ajé tó kọjá ó lọ sí Ilé Funfun Bbáláú, láàrin àwọn ìròyìn pé ó tí fẹ́ kswé fi ipò rẹ̀ sílẹ̀
rows.output: But on the next day, he went to the White House, between the news that he had resigned from his position
rows.reference: But last Monday he went to the White House, amid reports he was about to resign.

rows.source: Dípò, ìpàdé pẹ̀lú Trump, ẹni tí ó wà ní ìpàdé Àjọ ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé ní New York ní àkókò náà, di kíkéde láti wáyé ní ọjọ́’rú.
rows.output: Instead, the meeting with Trump, who was at the United Nations General Assembly in New York at the time, was canceled.
rows.reference: Instead, a meeting with Trump, who was then at the United Nations in New York, was announced for Thursday.

rows.source: Trump sọ pé òun "kò ní fẹ́" láti dá Rosenstein dúró lẹ́nu iṣẹ́ ṣùgbọ́n lẹ́yìn èyí ìpàdé náà di dídá dúró díẹ̀ láti yàgò fún èdè àìyedè pẹ̀lú ìgbìmọ̀ ìdájọ́ Aṣòfin àgbà ní ibi tí Kavanaugh àti ọ̀kan lára àwọn obìnrin tí ó fi ẹ̀sùn ìbálòpọ̀ ní ọ́nà àìtọ́ kan Ọ̀mọ̀wé Christine Blassey Ford, àwọn méjèèjì ló jẹ́ ẹ̀rí
rows.output: Trump said he "doesn't want" to fire Rosenstein but after the meeting it was decided to delay the confirmation of Kavanaugh and one of the women accusing him of sexual misconduct, Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, both of whom were to testify before the Senate.
rows.reference: Trump said he would "prefer not" to fire Rosenstein but then the meeting was delayed to avoid a clash with the Senate judiciary committee hearing in which Kavanaugh and one of the women who have accused him of sexual misconduct, Dr Christine Blasey Ford, both testified.

rows.source: Ní ọjọ́ ẹtì, Trump pa àṣẹ fún FBI láti ṣe ìwádìí ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanugh, tí ó tún mú kí ìdádúró wá fún píparí ìbò Ilé Aṣòfin àgbà.
rows.output: On Thursday, Trump ordered the FBI to investigate the allegations against Kavanaugh, which also delayed the final vote in the Senate.

rows.output: The Democrats, in short, are on a mission to "abolish" the Electoral College.
rows.reference: Democrats, he said, are on a mission to "resist and obstruct."

rows.source: “Kuma kun ga cewa a cikin kwanaki huɗu da suka wuce,” inji shi, yana mai kiran ‘yan Democrat ɗin da “masu fushi da baƙin ciki da zali da rashin gaskiya.”
rows.output: “And you have seen that in the last four days,” he said, calling the Democrats “angry and bitter and vengeful and untruthful.”
rows.reference: "And you see that over the last four days," he said, calling the Democrats "angry and mean and nasty and untruthful."

rows.source: Ya ambaci babban dan Kwamitin Shari’a na Majalisar Dattawa Sanata Dianne Feinstein da sunanta, wanda masu sauraro suka yi wa ihu.
rows.output: He mentioned the name of the Chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, Senator Dianne Feinstein, which the audience responded to with cheers.
rows.reference: He referenced Senate Judiciary Committee ranking Democratic Sen. Dianne Feinstein by name, which received loud boos from the audience.

rows.source: “Kun tuna amsarta?
rows.output: "Do you remember her answer?"
