rows.source: An yi shekaru goma tun lokacin da yankin kudancin New York ya kaddamar da hukuncin kisa.
rows.output: Ten years have passed since the southern New York region implemented the death penalty.
rows.reference: It has been a decade since the Southern District of New York last prosecuted a death penalty case.

rows.source: Wanda aka gurfanar da shi, Khalid Barnes, an yanke masa hukunci ne game da kashe masu raba kwaya biyu, amma an yanke masa hukuncin kisa a watan Satumba na 2009.
rows.output: The defendant, Khalid Barnes, was sentenced to death for the murders of two gay men, but was executed in September 2009.
rows.reference: The defendant, Khalid Barnes, was convicted of murdering two drug suppliers but was ultimately sentenced to life in prison in September 2009.

rows.source: karshen a lokacin da aka yanke hukuncin kisa a tarayya New York a 1953 ga Julius da Ethel Rosenberg, ma'aurata bayan da aka yanke musu hukuncin kulla makirci don Tarayyar Soviet a lokacin Yakin Tsana shekaru biyu da suka gabata.
rows.output: The end of the era of capital punishment in the United States came in 1953 with the execution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple who were sentenced to death for conspiracy to commit espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War, two years after their conviction.
rows.reference: The last time the death penalty was carried out in a New York federal case was in 1953 for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple executed after they were convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War two years before.

rows.source: Dukansu Rosenbergs sun mutu ne ta hanyar kujerar lantarki ranar 19 ga Yuni, 1953.
rows.output: Both Rosenbergs were executed by electric chair on June 19, 1953.
rows.reference: Both Rosenbergs were both put to death by the electric chair on June 19, 1953.

rows.source: Saipov, dan kasar Uzbekistan, ya nuna rashin tausayi a cikin kwanaki da watanni bayan harin, bisa ga takardun kotu.
rows.output: Saipov, a citizen of Uzbekistan, showed no remorse in the days and months following the attack, according to court documents.
rows.reference: Saipov, a native of Uzbekistan, demonstrated a lack of remorse in the days and months following the attack, according to court documents.

rows.source: Ya bayyana wa masu binciken cewa ya jin daɗin abin da ya yi, 'yan sanda sun ce.
rows.output: He told the investigators that he enjoyed what he was doing, the police said.
rows.reference: He stated to investigators that he felt good about what he had done, police said.

rows.source: Saipov ya shaida wa hukumomin da cewa ya samu kwarin guiwa bayan gudanar da harin bayan ya duba bidiyon ISIS a wayarsa, bisa ga zargin.
rows.output: Saipov told the authorities that he had received inspiration after conducting the attack after watching an ISIS video on his phone, according to the indictment.
rows.reference: Saipov told authorities he was inspired to carry out the attack after watching ISIS videos on his phone, according to the indictment.

rows.source: Har ila yau, ya bukaci a nuna tutar Isis a cikin dakin asibiti, in ji 'yan sanda.
rows.output: In addition, he demanded that the Isis flag be displayed in the hospital, the police said.
rows.reference: He also requested to display the ISIS flag in his hospital room, police said.

rows.source: Ya yi zargin ba shi da laifi ga tuhuma 22 na zargin.
rows.output: He was accused of being innocent of charges 22 of accusations.
rows.reference: He has pleaded not guilty to the 22-count indictment.

rows.source: David Patton, daya daga cikin masu kare hakkin jama'a na tarayya a jihar Saipov, ya ce su na da "takaici" tare da yanke shawara.
rows.output: David Patton, one of the national security lawyers in the Saipov case, said they were "disappointed" with the ruling.
rows.reference: David Patton, one of the federal public defenders representing Saipov, said they are "obviously disappointed" with the prosecution's decision.

rows.source: "Mu na tsammanin shawarar da za a nemi hukuncin kisa maimakon karɓar laifin mai laifi zuwa rai a kurkuku ba tare da yiwuwar saki ba zai shawo kan matsalolin abubuwan da ke faruwa ga kowa da kowa", inji Patton.
rows.output: "We expect that the recommendation for a death sentence instead of a life sentence for a convicted person will address the problems of the current situation for everyone," said Patton.
rows.reference: "We think the decision to seek the death penalty rather than accepting a guilty plea to life in prison with no possibility of release will only prolong the trauma of these events for everyone involved," Patton said.

rows.source: Lauyoyi masu kare Saipov sun nemi masu gabatar da kara kada su nemi hukuncin kisa.
rows.output: The defense lawyers for Saipov requested the prosecution not to seek the death penalty.
rows.reference: Saipov's defense team had previously asked prosecutors not to seek the death penalty.

rows.source: Tory MP ya ce NIGEL FARAGE ya kamata a kula da tattaunawar Brexit
rows.output: Tory MP says NIGEL FARAGE should be in charge of the Brexit talks

rows.output: It is a very serious matter that the tolerance for different views in the Labour Party is not accepted, and any idea is suppressed and must be accepted in the party's leadership.

rows.output: This began immediately Jeremy became leader, my colleagues, those I thought I shared a common understanding of politics with, started to look at me and I would turn around and take positions that I would not have agreed with any of them - either on national security or on the EU market.
rows.reference: This started shortly after Jeremy became leader, as colleagues with whom I had previously thought I shared a similar political outlook began expecting me to do a U-turn and take positions I would never have otherwise agreed with - whether on national security or the EU single market.

rows.output: Whenever I speak at a public event - it will not be in response to what I said - there is a great deal of pressure to follow up with a call for unity, criticism of the political center, and my character that I should not be in the Labor Party.
rows.reference: Whenever I speak publicly - and it doesn't really matter what I say - there follows a tirade of abuse on social media calling for deselection, denouncing the politics of the centre, telling me I should not be in the Labour party.

rows.output: I've had a lot of advice over the past two years to be humble and to stop talking so much, and I've been told, "You won't have any problems."

rows.source: Mana nke ahụ abụghị ihe m banyere ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị ịme.
rows.output: But that's not what I'm about in politics.

rows.source: Kemgbe m sonyere Labour afọ 32 ka nwa akwụkwọ, nke nlegharị anya gọọmentị Thatcher kpalitere, nke hapụrụ ime ụlọ akwụkwọ m na nnukwu mmebi, achọrọ m na mbụ idu ọrụ mara mma nke ọhaneze maka ndị kachasị chọọ ha - ma abụ m onye ndu obere mpaghara ma ọ bụ minista gọọmentị.
rows.output: Since I joined the Labour Party 32 years ago as a student, the Thatcher government's policies of marketization and privatization left my school in a state of disrepair, I initially wanted to lead a public service that was truly needed by those who needed it most - and I was a local council leader or a government minister.
rows.reference: Ever since I joined Labour 32 years ago as a school pupil, provoked by the Thatcher government's neglect that had left my comprehensive school classroom literally falling down, I've sought to champion better public services for those who need them most - whether as a local councillor or government minister.

rows.source: Ezobeghị m ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị m na mbụ, gụnyere ntuli aka ikpeazụ.
rows.output: I have not been involved in politics before, including the last election.

rows.source: Ọnweghị onye ọ bụla nọ na Nottingham East ga-enwe mgbagwoju anya gbasara ọnọdụ iwu m yana mpaghara ndị mụ ekwenyeghị n’ọchịchị dị ugbu a.

rows.source: Maka ndị ahụ kwadoro ụkpụrụ ahụ na Fraịde, ihe niile m nwere ike ikwu bụ na mgbe obodo na aga ịnwe Brexit ga-enwe mmetụta adịghị mma n’ọtụtụ ezinụlọ, azụmahịa na ọrụ ọhaneze anyị, aghọtaghị m agụụ iji gbuo oge na ike maka nkwado m na ndị isi ndọrọndọrọ Labour.
rows.output: For those who supported the motion on Friday, all I can say is that when the country goes through Brexit, it will have a negative impact on many families, businesses, and public services in our country, I do not understand the appetite to waste time and energy in supporting my motion and the leadership of the Labour Party.

rows.source: Ịgba mbọ hụ na inwetara ụra zuru ezu, dị mma, kwesịrị ịbụ ngwa agha nwata akwụkwọ’ iji chere mgbakasị ahụ, ike ọgwụgwụ na obi mmapụ aka mgba, o kwuru - ọbụlagodi izenari ntinye ahụ, ka arahụghị ụra na-etinye ụbụrụ n’ọnọdụ oke agụụ, na-eme ha agụụ kwa mgbe.
rows.output: Ensure you get enough, good quality sleep, as it is a weapon against the fatigue, stress and anxiety, he said - even if you are not getting enough sleep, your brain is in a state of extreme hunger, making you feel hungry all the time.
rows.reference: Ensuring you have enough sleep, of a good quality, should be a student's 'secret weapon' to combat stress, exhaustion and anxiety, he said - even to avoid putting on weight, as sleep deprivation puts the brain into starvation mode, making them constantly hungry.

rows.source: Raymond So, nwata gbara afọ 19 nke California na-agụ kemikal na fisikal baịyọlọji nyere Ọkammụta Czeisler aka ịhazi mmụta ahụ, ebe o megoro otu klaasị ya n’afọ gara aga n’ime oge afọ izizi ya na Harvard.
rows.output: Raymond So, a 19-year-old student from California who is studying chemistry and physics at Caltech, helped Professor Czeisler organize the study, as he had taken one of his classes the previous year during his freshman year at Harvard.

rows.output: Dr. Czeisler advised students to consider wearing glasses for when they need to rest their eyes, and when they need to get up, and to be aware of the potential negative effects of the "blue light" emitted by electronic devices on their sleep patterns and the sleep cycle.

rows.source: Ọ bụ omenala ugbu a ịchọ mkpa Brexit n’ihe nkiri ọhụrụ ọ bụla nwere nribama Britain, na nke a dịka ọ metụtara mmegharị ihe nkiri ịkpa ọchị nke Johnny English - bụ nke ejiri Johnny English malite na 2003, wee laghachikwa azụ na 2011 ka Johnny English Reborn.
rows.output: It is now a trend to demand Brexit in every new film with a British cast, and this one is no exception. This trend is particularly evident in the comedy film Johnny English, which was first introduced in 2003 and then returned in 2011 as Johnny English Reborn.
rows.reference: It's traditional now to look for Brexit significances in any new film with a British slant and that does seem applicable to this revival of the Johnny English action-comedy spoof franchise - which started back in 2003 with Johnny English and spluttered back to life in 2011 with Johnny English Reborn.

rows.source: Ọ pụtara na ihe nkiri njakịrị nke isiokwu otu anyị siri bụrụ ndị iberibe pụtara ihie, bụzi oghere nbufe ahịa ọhụrụ anyị?
rows.output: It appeared in a comedy film with the theme of how we became the idiots, is it a new business opportunity?
rows.reference: Will tongue-in-cheek self-satire on the subject of how obviously rubbish we are be the nation's new export opportunity?

rows.source: Kosiladị, onye nzuzu anya ọkpụ, ihu rọba Johnny English emegharịala ikike ya ịkwalite ihe nke ugboro abụọ - aha ya karịa ihe ọ bụla na-egosi na ọ bụ nchepụta ihe ịkpa ọchị emebere maka akụkụ obodo ndị anaghị asụ Bekee.
rows.output: However, the ridiculous, plastic face of Johnny English has once again failed to improve its already laughable status - a parody of a parody made for the non-English speaking parts of the world.
rows.reference: At any rate, the pop-eyed, rubber-faced incompetent Johnny English has had his licence to cock things up renewed for the second time - that name of his signalling more than anything else that he is a broad comic creation designed for non-English-speaking cinemagoing territories.

rows.source: N’ezie ọ bụ onye iberibe ọrụ nzuzo nke agbanyeghị ṅṅomi ya gbagwojuru anya, nwere obere Clouseau, ntakịrị Mr Bean na nfechalụ nke nwoke ahụ n’etinye otu olu na isiokwu Chariots of Fire na mmalite mmemme Olympics London 2012.
rows.output: Of course, he is a clumsy secret agent, but he is a parody of himself, with a little Clouseau, a little Mr. Bean, and the awkwardness of the man who puts one voice on the theme of Chariots of Fire and the opening ceremony of the London 2012 Olympics.
rows.reference: He is of course the daft secret agent who despite his bizarre pretensions to smoothie glamour has got a little bit of Clouseau, a dash of Mr Bean and a dollop of that chap contributing a single note to the Chariots of Fire theme tune at the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony.

rows.source: N’izizi ọ dabere n’onye njem yana nwoke nzuzo mba ụwa Atkinson nke emere na ihe mgbasa ozi Barclaycard TV echefugoro, na-ahapu ọgbaghara n’azụ ya.
rows.output: In the beginning, you were based on the world traveler and international man of mystery Atkinson, who was featured in a series of Barclaycard TV commercials, and who left a trail of chaos in his wake.

rows.output: I liked Johnny English getting close to the plane where the old army uniforms, the fanfare was blowing on his helmet.
rows.reference: I loved Johnny English approaching a helicopter while dressed in a medieval suit of armour and the rotor blades briefly clanging against his helmet.

rows.source: Onyinye Atkinson nwere maka ịkpa ọchị a na-ahụ anya pụtara ihie, mana ịkpa ọchị ahụ esighi ike ma mafee oke, tụmadị ihe nkiri ndị ahụ “anaghị akpa ọchị” dịka 007 na Mission Impossible n’onwe ha na-enwekwa ihe ịkpa ọchị n’ime ya ugbu a.
rows.output: Atkinson's award for this visually driven comedy was well-deserved, but the comedy itself was weak and overdone, making the films "not funny" like 007 and Mission Impossible, which now also have comedy in them.
rows.reference: Atkinson's gift for physical comedy is on display, but the humour feels pretty underpowered and weirdly superfluous, especially as the "serious" film brands like 007 and Mission Impossible themselves now confidently offer comedy as an ingredient.

rows.source: Ihe ịkpa ọchị ahụ dịka ọ bụ ụmụaka ka emebere ya karịa ndị okenye, maka mụ onwe m njegheri Johnny English enweghị ihe nchepụta pụrụ iche yana ebumnuche ya dịka ihe nkiri anaghị ekwu okwu nke Atkinson, n’onye nke Bean.
rows.output: The comedy is more childlike than for adults, for myself I found Johnny English lacking in originality and purpose as a non-verbal comedy film of Atkinson, in whom Bean excels.
rows.reference: The humour feels as if it is pitched at kids rather than adults, and for me Johnny English's wacky misadventures aren't as inventive and focused as Atkinson's silent-movie gags in the persona of Bean.

rows.source: U.S. Onye Isi Ala Donald Trump na Wenesde gara aga rụtụrụ aka na mgbakwunye akwụrụ ụgwọ nke China Daily na Des Moines Register - akwụkwọ akụkọ obodo Iowa kacha ere ahịa - ka o bochara China ebubo ịchọ itinye aka na ntuli aka ndị ọmebe iwu U.S na Nọvemba 6, ebubo nke China gọnarịrị.
rows.output: On Wednesday, U.S. President Donald Trump accused China of attempting to influence the midterm elections in the United States on November 6, a claim that China has denied.
rows.reference: U.S. President Donald Trump last Wednesday referred to the China Daily's paid supplement in the Des Moines Register - the state of Iowa's biggest selling newspaper - after accusing China of seeking to meddle in the Nov. 6 U.S. congressional elections, a charge China denies.

rows.source: Ebubo Trump na Beijing na-agbalị itinye aka na ntuli aka U.S gosiri ihe ndị ọrụ U.S gwara ndị Reuters na ọ bụ agba nke ọhụrụ na mgbakiri ala Washington na-abawanye ịkwagide China.
rows.output: Trump's allegations that Beijing is trying to interfere in the U.S. election reflect a new level of escalation in the Washington-Washington conflict over China.
rows.reference: Trump's accusation that Beijing was trying to meddle in U.S. elections marked what U.S. officials told Reuters was a new phase in an escalating campaign by Washington to put pressure on China.

rows.source: Ebe ọ bụ ihe nkiti gọọmentị mba ofesi itinye mgbasa ozi iji kwalite ahịa, Beijing na Washington nọ na ndọrọndọrọ azụmahịa na-abawanye nke megoro ka ha tinye ụtụ ngwahịa na ahịa mbubadata ha.
rows.output: The government has been using propaganda to promote trade, and Beijing and Washington have been increasing their trade relations, which have led to the imposition of tariffs on their imports.
rows.reference: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.

rows.source: Ntinye ụtụ ngwahịa nke China mere na mbido agha azụmahịa ka emebere ka ọ metụta ndị na ebupu ahịa n’obodo dịka Iowa kwadoro otu ndọrọndọrọ Repọblikan nke Trump, ndị ọkammara China na U.S kwuru.
rows.output: The Chinese trade war tariffs were designed to hurt American exporters like Iowa, said Republican lawmakers, according to Chinese experts.
rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Terry Branstad, onye nnọchite anya U.S na China bụkwa onye chịburu Iowa, onye mbupu ahịa nri ubi nke ukwuu na China, kwuru na China merụrụ ndị ọrụ, ndị ọrụ ugbo na azụmahịa nke America ahụ.
rows.output: Terry Branstad, the U.S. Trade Representative and former governor of Iowa, which is a major exporter of agricultural products to China, said that China has harmed American workers, farmers, and businesses.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: China, Branstad dere n’echiche ya na Des Moines Register na Sọnde, “na-ekwusi ike maka mmegide ahụ site na itinye mgbasa ozi n’akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi anyị.”
rows.output: China, Branstad wrote in his column for the Des Moines Register on Sunday, "emphasized the opposition by placing ads in our newspapers."
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: “N’ịgbasa ozi asị a, gọọmentị China na ewere oghere omenala America hụrụ n’anya bụ nke onye kwuo uche ya na mgbasa ozi enweghị mkpagbu were tinye mgbasa ozi akwụrụ ụgwọ na Des Moines Register.” Branstad dere.
rows.output: “In spreading this false information, the Chinese government is taking advantage of the cultural openness of the United States, which is a democratic country with a free press, to insert paid advertising in the Des Moines Register.” Branstad wrote.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: “Ma ịtụlee ya n’ọdụ akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi dị n’okporo beijing ebe a, ịga ahụ na enwere obere olu ndịiche nke na ịghaghị ahụ ihe n’egosi n’ezie echiche di iche ndị China nwere ike nwee maka usoro akụnụba China nọ na nsogbu, ebe ọ bụ n’ụlọ mgbasa ozi nọ na njikwa nke China Communist Party,” ọ dere.
rows.output: But consider this: at the Beijing news media center, you can see that there is a small minority of dissenting voices that are not being heard, and this is really a reflection of the fact that the Chinese people may have different views on the Chinese economic system that is in crisis, because the media is under the control of the Chinese Communist Party.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na “otu n’ime akwụkwọ akụkọ ama ama na China zenarịrị ibiputa” ederede ya, n’agbanyeghị na o kwughị akwụkwọ akụkọ nke ọ bụ.
rows.output: He also added that "one of the most popular Chinese novels that has escaped censorship" is his writing, although he did not mention the novel.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ndị Repọblikan Na-akpachapụ Ndị Ntuli Aka Ụmụ-nwanyị Tupu Ntuli Aka Ọkara Ọchịchị Maka Ọgbaghara Kavanaugh, Ndị Nyocha Dọrọ Aka na Ntị
rows.output: The Republican Party's Handling of Sexual Assault Allegations Against Kavanaugh, a Threat to Women's Rights, and the Need for a New Political Party
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Dị ka ọtụtụ ndị isi Repọblikan kwụnyere ma kwuchitere Onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu Brett Kavanaugh n’ihu ebubo dị iche iche nke mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị, ndị nyocha adọọla aka na ntị na ha ga-ahụ ndapụta iwe ga-esite ọkachasị n’aka ụmụ-nwanyị, n’oge ntuli aka ọkara ọchịchị na-abịa.
rows.output: Like many Republican leaders who supported and defended Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh amid various sexual misconduct allegations, investigators have warned that they will be looking for signs of increased aggression, especially from women, in the upcoming midterm elections.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Mmetụta sochiri nke a dị elu nke ukwuu, na ọtụtụ ndị Repọblikan ka edekọbara na ha egosila na ha chọrọ ịga n’ihu mee ntuli aka.
rows.output: The consequences of this are extremely serious, and many Republicans have been recorded as saying that they want to go ahead and hold elections.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Enweghị ike iweghachi ihe ndị ahụ,” Grant Reeher, onye ọkammụta nke sayensị ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na Syracuse University Maxwell School gwara The Hill maka ederede nke ebiputara na Satọde.
rows.output: The Hill reported on Saturday that Grant Reeher, a political science professor at Syracuse University's Maxwell School, said, "The things that are lost can't be recovered."
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reeher kwuru na ya na-agbagha n’ọkwụkwa ikpeazụ nke Onye Ọmebe Iwu Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) mere maka nyocha FBI a ga-ezu iji wetuo iwe ndị ntuli aka.
rows.output: Reeher said he was disappointed in the last-minute move by Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) to hold up the FBI investigation that would have been used to discredit the voters.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: “Ụmụ-nwanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụnyahụ - ha agaghị echefu echi niile ma Nọvemba, “ Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ senịọ na onye nkwuchite okwu obodo maka otu ọganihu MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dabere na akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday - they will not forget tomorrow and November," said Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, on Friday, based on a report from the Washington, D.C.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: N’ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị ngagharị iwe kwere ukwe “Nọvemba na-abịa!” ka ha na-agagharị ngagharị iwe n’ogologo ụzọ Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu ebe ndị Repọblikan ji Ọgbakọ Ọka Ikpe họrọ ịga n’ihu na nhọrọ Kavanaugh agbanyeghị nkwuputa Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kwuputara.
rows.output: On Friday morning, protesters chanted "November is coming!" as they marched through the streets of Capitol Hill where Republicans were poised to advance Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, reported Mic.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: “Ịnụ ọkụ n’obi na mkpalite mmụọ nke Demokrat ga-apụ iche,” Stu Rothenberg, onye nyocha ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị enweghị otu o binyere gwara ndị akụkọ.
rows.output: "The enthusiasm and spiritual awakening of the Democrats will be different," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told reporters.
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: “Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke a bụ eziokwu.
rows.output: "People say it's high; this is true."
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Mana ọ nwere ike ịgbagokwu ọkachasị n’etiti ụmụ-nwanyị n’enweghị otu ha binyere n’ime obodo yana ndị ntuli aka na-etolite etolite, gbara afọ 18- ruo 29-, bụ ndị ebe onye isi ala anaghị amasị, anaghị eme ntuli aka kwa mgbe.”
rows.output: But you can talk most freely among women without any of them being registered in the city and the young voters, aged 18-29, who are not fond of the president, do not vote regularly.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Ọbụlagodi tupu nkwuputanke ọha Ford mere na-akọwa ebubo mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị megide onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe kachasị Elu, ndị nyocha na-atụ elo na ndapụta iwe nwere ike sote ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Repọblikan gaa n’ihu mee nkwado ahụ.
rows.output: Before Ford's public statement, describing the sexual harassment allegations against the Supreme Court nominee, investigators were speculating that a backlash could follow if Republicans proceeded with the confirmation.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Nke a abụrụla ọgbaghara dịịrị GOP,” Michael Steele kwuru, onye isi chịburu Ọgbakọ Otu Repọblikan, na mbido izug ara aga, dabere na NBC News.
rows.output: "This has been a disaster for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, at the beginning of the year, based on NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.
rows.output: "It's not just about the primaries or the general election, but also about how the Republicans are handling this and how they are treating it," Guy Cecil, the head of Priorities USA, a Democratic group, told reporters.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.output: Kaosadị, ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n'onye ha ga-ekwenye na ndị na-akwado Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwadoro onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.
rows.output: A new survey from YouGov found that 41% of respondents completely agree or somewhat agree with Ford's statement, while 35% completely agree or somewhat agree with Kavanaugh's statement.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.
rows.output: In addition, 38 percent said they believed that Kavanaugh was probably lying or completely untruthful during his testimony, while only 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.
rows.output: After Flake's acquittal, the FBI is currently investigating Ford's allegations, as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.
rows.output: Ford made a statement in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh assaulted her in an intoxicated state when she was 17 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez was accused by the Supreme Court nominee of being too aggressive when they were classmates at Yale in the 1980s.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook
rows.output: The World Wide Web Inventor Announces New Internet Plan to Join Google and Facebook
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, starts a new company that will compete with Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.output: The new plan, Inrupt, is a startup that is pushing the boundaries of the open-source software that Berners-Lee founded, Solid.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.
rows.output: Solid provides users with the flexibility to choose where they store their data and the information that people can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”
rows.output: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the purpose of Inrupt was "to take over the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
rows.output: "We will do it now," he said of the new house.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”
rows.output: "It's time to sign up for the story."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid enye ndị mmadụ oghere imepụta “ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị” ma ọ bụ POD.
rows.output: The device uses Solid technology to give people the opportunity to create their own "personal online data storage" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: It can have a contact list, a to-do list, a calendar, a music player, and personal and work apps.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n’otu nchọgharị ma ha niile n’otu oge.
rows.output: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify all in one search and all at once.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.
rows.output: The unique thing about private data storage on the internet is that it is up to the person who owns it to decide who gets to access the information.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”
rows.output: The company calls it "personalization from data."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.
rows.output: Inrupt's mission, based on CEO John Bruce, is to bring together companies, infrastructure, systems, and skills to help make Solid accessible to everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.
rows.output: The company was only Berners-Lee, Bruce, and the IBM storage division that had been acquired, along with a team of engineers working on the project, and a group of volunteer coders.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.
rows.output: By next week, global tech producers will be able to create decentralized applications using the decentralized app framework on Inrupt's website.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that his team was not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether they would start or abandon the new beginning where the business model is immediately turned on its head."
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”
rows.output: "We do not accept them."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”
rows.output: In a Medium post on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that "Inrupt's goal is to give power to commerce and the environment to help keep trust and integrity in the new web that we've built on Solid."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee revolutionized the Internet by creating the World Wide Web Consortium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.
rows.output: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal advocate for the freedom of the internet.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.output: The UK "will be disappointed to miss out" on the chance to be a global leader in car manufacturing if Brexit goes ahead, Trade Secretary Greg Clark said.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na ọ bụ ihe “na-atụ uche” na Toyota UK gwara BBC na ọ bụrụ na Britain apụọ na EU na-enweghị nkwekọrịta, na ha ga-akwụsị nwa oge ịrụpụta ihe n’ụlọ nrụpụta dị na Burnaston, n’akụkụ Derby.
rows.output: He added that it was "disappointing" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal, they would temporarily stop production at their plant in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: “Anyị chọrọ nkwekọrịta,” Mr Clark kwuru.
rows.output: "We want a contract," Mr. Clark said.

rows.source: Onye ọrụ ụgbọ ala nke Japan ahụ kwuru na ndapụta nke igbu oge n’oke ala ma ọ bụrụ na enweghị nkwekọrịta Brexit nwere ike napụ ọrụ.
rows.output: The Japanese truck driver said that delays in the Brexit negotiations could cost him his job.

rows.source: Ụlọ nrụpụta nke Burnaston - bụ nke na-arụpụta Toyota Auris na Avensis - rụpụtara ihe ruru ụgbọ ala 150,000 n’afọ gara aga nke ebupuru 90% ya na mba European Union ndị ọzọ.
rows.output: The Burnaston plant - which manufactures the Toyota Auris and Avensis - produced around 150,000 vehicles last year, with 90% of those exported to other European Union countries.
rows.reference: The Burnaston plant - which makes Toyota's Auris and Avensis - produced nearly 150,000 cars last year of which 90% were exported to the rest of the European Union.

rows.source: “Echiche m bụ na ọ bụrụ na Britain apụọ na EU na ngwucha Maachị, anyị ga-ahụ na nrụpụta kwụsịrị n’ụlọ nrụpụta anyị” Marvin Cooke onye isi njikwa Toyota na Burnaston kwuru.
rows.output: "My view is that if Britain leaves the EU at the end of March, we will see production stop at our plants," said Marvin Cooke, managing director of Toyota in Burnaston.
rows.reference: "My view is that if Britain crashes out of the EU at the end of March we will see production stops in our factory," said Marvin Cooke, Toyota's managing director at Burnaston.

rows.source: Ndị ọzọ na-arụpụta ụgbọ ala na UK na-atụ egwu banyere ịhapụ EU na-enweghị nkwekọrịta ka azụmahịa na-agafe oke ala ga-esi rụọ ọrụ, tinyere Honda, BMW na Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.output: Other UK car manufacturers are concerned about leaving the EU without a deal, as they fear that trade across borders will not function properly, including Honda, BMW, and Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.reference: Other UK car manufacturers have raised fears about leaving the EU without agreement on how cross-border trade will function, including Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.

rows.source: BMW, maka ọmụmatụ, kwuru na ya ga-emechi Obere ụlọ nrụpụta ya dị na Oxford maka otu ọnwa ma emechaa Brexit.
rows.output: BMW, for example, said it would close its Mini plant in Oxford for one month and then reassess Brexit.
rows.reference: BMW, for example, says it will close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month following Brexit.

rows.source: Mkpatụta kacha gbasara ihe ndị na-arụ ụgbọ ala kwuru bụ n’ihe egwu mbunye ahịa ma ọ bụrụ na enwetaghị nkwekọrịta.
rows.output: The most significant concern of the taxi drivers was the risk of a cartel if no agreement was reached.
rows.reference: The main concerns relate to what carmakers say are supply chain risks in the event of a no-deal Brexit.

rows.source: A na-eme nrụpụta na Toyota n’ahiri usoro “ọ bịa ozugbo”, ebe akụkụ ụgbọ ala na-eji nkeji 37 nwere esi n’aka ndị mbunye ahịa abịa, ma UK na EU maka ụgbọ ala atụrụ ahịa ya.
rows.output: We produce at Toyota on a "just-in-time" basis, where parts for vehicles arrive in 37 minutes from suppliers, and for our European market, both in the UK and EU.
rows.reference: Toyota's production line is run on a "just-in-time" basis, with parts arriving every 37 minutes from suppliers in both the UK and the EU for cars made to order.

rows.source: Ọ bụrụ na UK ahapụ EU n’enwetaghị nkwekọrịta na Maachị 29, enwere ike inwe ọgbaghara n’oke ala bụ nke ụlọ nrụpụta kwuru na ọ nwere ike bute igbu oge yana ezughị ezu akụkụ ụgbọ ala.
rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on March 29, there could be a shortage of parts on the assembly line, which the car industry said could lead to delays and incomplete vehicles.
rows.reference: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on 29 March, there could be disruption at the border which the industry says could lead to delays and shortages of parts.

rows.source: Ọ gaghị ekwe omume na Toyota ga-ahapụ ngwaahịa  karịrị nke otu ụbọchị n’ụlọ nrụpụta ha dị na Derbyshire, ụlọ ọrụ ahụ kwuru, yamere na nrụpụta ga-akwụsị.
rows.output: It is impossible for Toyota to leave more than one day's worth of products at their Derbyshire factory, the company said, given that production will cease.

rows.source: Mr Clark kwuru na atụmatụ Chequers nke Theresa May maka mmekọrịta ha na EU n’ọdịnihu bụ “nke emebere ka ọ zenarị nyocha niile ahụ n’oke ala.”
rows.output: Mr. Clark said that Theresa May's Chequers plan for future UK-EU relations was "designed to avoid any scrutiny at all."

rows.source: “Anyị chọrọ inwe nkwekọrịta.   Anyị chọrọ inwe nkwekọrịta kacha mma ga-enye anyị oghere dịka m na-ekwu, nke abụghị naanị inweta ọganihu ugbu a ma ka anyị jidekwa oghere a,” ọ gwara ihe mmemme BBC Radio 4 Today.
rows.output: "We want a deal. We want the best possible deal that will give us the space I'm talking about, which is not just about getting growth now but also keeping that space."
rows.reference: "We need to have a deal. We want to have the best deal that will allow as I say not just the success at present to be enjoyed but for us to grasp this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

rows.source: “Akaebe sitere n’abụghị naanị Toyota ma ndị ọzọ na-eme nrụpụta bụ na ekwesịrị ịga n’ihu soro usoro mbunye ahịa nke na-aga nke ọma kpamkpam.”
rows.output: "Testimony from not only Toyota but also other manufacturers is that we need to continue with the successful importation process."

rows.output: Toyota cannot yet say how long it will take to stop production, but in the meantime, they are warning that additional price increases will weaken its competitiveness and eventually lead to job losses.

rows.output: But we will see, I always like to make the media aware of what is happening immediately.

rows.output: The president has more time for press conferences than any president before him, "he said, adding that "we have seen the numbers."

rows.output: We have been trying to do that many times, you have seen us do that a few weeks ago, that will be the summary of the report when you can talk to the President of the United States.

rows.output: Harris said, "There has been no explanation in terms of the nature/extent of the injury" with the Tennessee State and trying to figure out when the injury occurred.

rows.output: For many people, the dream of owning their own home is still a distant reality, the scourge of homelessness is a harsh reminder.

rows.output: Sunderland's head coach Jack Ross said his "biggest wish" was to be Scotland's manager one day.
rows.reference: Sunderland boss Jack Ross says his "ultimate ambition" is to become the Scotland manager at some stage.

rows.source: Onye Scotland ahụ, 42, na enwe obi ụtọ maka mgba nke iweghachite otu asọmpi North-East, ndị nọ ugbu a n’ọkwa atọ na League One, akara atọ n’okpuru nke isi.
rows.output: The 42-year-old Scot is delighted with the challenge of trying to bring the North-East title back to the club, who are currently third in League One, three points off the top.
rows.reference: The Scot, 42, is relishing the challenge of reviving the North-East club, who currently sit third place in League One, three points off the top.

rows.reference: He moved to the Stadium of Light this summer after guiding St Mirren back to the Scottish Premiership last season.

rows.output: I got the B cap and that was it," Ross told Sportsound of BBC Scotland.

rows.source: “Mana etolitere m na elele Scotland na Hampden ọtụtụ oge, mụ na nna m ka m bụ nwata, ọ bụ ihe na adọghachi m oge niile.
rows.output: But I grew up watching Scotland at Hampden many times, with my dad when I was a kid, and it's something that brings me back every time.

rows.reference: Ross's predecessors as Sunderland manager include Dick Advocaat, David Moyes, Sam Allardyce, Martin O'Neill, Roy Keane, Gus Poyet and Paulo Di Canio.

rows.output: The former head of Alloa Athletic said he was not afraid to follow in the footsteps of the famous names in the big club's history, after being asked by fans from Barnsley and Ipswich Town.

rows.source: “Ọganihu maka m n’oge a ka a ga-atụ site na “enwere m ike idughachi otu a na Premier League?’
rows.output: “Progress for me at this time is to be measured by ‘can I turn this team around in the Premier League?’
rows.reference: "Success for me at the moment will be gauged by 'can I return this club to the Premier League?'

rows.source: N’ihi nyiwe na ụlọ nke otu a, na enweghị mgbagha kwesịrị ịnọ na Premier League,” o kwuru.

rows.output: "It's not easy to get back to that place, but I can only imagine myself as the person who succeeded there if I can recreate that same team there."
rows.reference: "It is not an easy task to get it there, but I would probably only view myself as being successful here if I can get the club back there."

rows.source: Ross nọ naanị afọ atọ n’ọrụ njikwa ya, ka obere oge gachara ka onye enyemaka na Dumbarton yana ọnụnọ ọnwa 15 n’otu ndị ọrụ Hearts.
rows.output: Ross was only three years into his management role, having served a brief stint as an assistant at Dumbarton and 15 months at Hearts.
rows.reference: Ross is only three years into his management career, after a period as assistant boss at Dumbarton and a 15-month spell on Hearts' coaching staff.

rows.output: He helped Alloa return to the third division, and led St Mirren from the bottom of the league to Championship cup victory in the following season.

rows.output: But Ross said he was more confident now than he was during his time with Clyde, Hartlepool, Falkirk, St Mirren and Hamilton Academical.
rows.reference: And Ross says he feels more comfortable now than he ever did during his playing career at Clyde, Hartlepool, Falkirk, St Mirren and Hamilton Academical.

rows.source: “Ọ nwere ike ịbụ ezi njikọ,” ọ chetere, ịweghara ikike na Alloa.

rows.source: “Ekwenyere n’ezie na njikwa bụ ihe ziri m nke ọma, karịa ịgba agba.

rows.source: Ọ dara ka ihe ọjọọ n’ihi na m mere nke ọma, ebiri ezigbo ndụ na ya, ma nwee ọhụụ ụfọdụ ihe ndị elu dị mma.
rows.output: It was a terrible thing because I had done well, I had plundered a good life from it, and had some visions of what was good.
rows.reference: It sounds bizarre because I did okay, made a reasonable living out of it, and enjoyed some reasonable highs.

rows.source: Mana ịgba agba na esi ike.

rows.reference: But playing can be tough.

rows.source: Enwere ọtụtụ ihe ị ga-agafere kwa izu.
rows.output: There are many things you will have to go through every week.
rows.reference: There are a lot of things you have to get through on a weekly basis.

rows.source: M ka na agafe nke ahụ n’okwu nke nsogbu na ndagide nke ọrụ ahụ mana njikwa dị mma n’anya.
rows.output: I'm still going through that in the context of the problem and the stability of the project, but the management is good in the sense.
rows.reference: I still go through that in terms of the stresses and pressure of the job but management just feels right.

rows.source: Bido na mbụ achọrọ m ịme njikwa, ugbu a ana m eme ya, ọ kachasị enye m mmetụta obi ume ala, abụ m onwe m na ndụ okenye m niile.”
rows.output: First, I wanted to be in control, now I am, and I feel the most alive, I am myself in my entire adult life.
rows.reference: I always wanted to manage and now I am doing it, it feels the most comfortable I have been in my own skin throughout my entire adult life."

rows.output: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi called the Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh "a threat to the Constitution" and said she was "furious" to work with him on the Court.
rows.reference: House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi called Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh "hysterical" and said that he was temperamentally unfit to serve on the Supreme Court.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru okwu ndị ahụ n’ajụjụ ọnụ na Satọde na Texas Tribune Festival na Austin, Texas.

rows.output: "I can't stop thinking that if a woman did that, they'd say 'headache,'" Pelosi said of her reaction to the testimony of Kavanaugh before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Thursday.

rows.source: Kavanaugh jiri nnukwu mwute gọnarị ebubo ndị ahụ na ọ wakporo Dk. Christine Blasey Ford n’ike mgbe ha abụọ bụ ndị ntorobịa.
rows.output: Kavanaugh denied the allegations of sexual assault against Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, which both were involved in as teenagers.
rows.reference: Kavanaugh emotionally denied allegations that he had sexually assaulted Dr. Christine Blasey Ford when they were both teenagers.

rows.source: N’oge nkwupute mmepe ya, mmụọ Kavanaugh di elu nke ukwuu, oge ụfọdụ ọ na achọ iti mkpu ma olu a na agbagbu ya ka ọ na ekwu maka ezinụlọ ya yana afọ ụlọ akwụkwọ kọleji ya.
rows.output: During his confirmation hearing, Kavanaugh's spirit was so high that at times he would want to scream and his voice would crack as he spoke about his family and his college years.
rows.reference: During his opening statement, Kavanaugh was very emotional, at times nearly shouting and choking up while discussing his family and his high school years.

rows.source: Ọ kọtọkwara ndị Demokrat nọ n’ọgbakọ ahụ n’ụzọ doro anya, na akpọ ebubo emere ya “mgbagbu omume dị egwu n’anya, akpara akpa” nke ndị mmesapụ ahụ na ewe iwe na Hillary Clinton dara na ntuli aka onye isi ala 2016 haziri.
rows.output: He clearly reached out to Democratic members of the committee, calling the allegations against him "a gross abuse of power, a slap in the face" of the committee members who were outraged by Hillary Clinton's defeat in the 2016 presidential election.
rows.reference: He also explicitly condemned Democrats on the committee, calling the allegations against him a "grotesque and coordinated character assassination" organized by liberals angry that Hillary Clinton lost the 2016 presidential election.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru na ọ kwenyere na akaebe nke Kavanaugh gosiri ọ nweghị ike ịrụ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị, n’ihi o gosiri na ọ nweghị mmasị n’ebe ndị Demokrat nọ.
rows.output: Pelosi said she believes the evidence of Kavanaugh shows that he is not capable of working in the Supreme Court, because it shows that he is not interested in the Democrats.
rows.reference: Pelosi said that she believed Kavanaugh's testimony proved that he could not serve on the Supreme Court, because it showed that he is biased against Democrats.

rows.source: O kwuru “echere m na ọ kagburu onwe ya site na iji okwu ndị ahụ yana n’ụzọ o si kwutọọ Clintons yana ndị Demokrat,”
rows.output: He said "I think he's self-destructing with the use of those words and the way he's attacking the Clintons and the Democrats."
rows.reference: "I think that he disqualifies himself with those statements and the manner in which he went after the Clintons and the Democrats," she said.

rows.source: Pelosi dajụrụ mgbe ajụrụ ma ọ ga-achọ iwepu Kavanaugh ma ọ bụrụ na etinye ya n’oche, ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Demokrat nweta ọnụọgụgụ karịrị na Ụlọ nke Ndị Nnọchite.
rows.output: Pelosi hesitated when asked if she would support removing Kavanaugh if he were confirmed, if the Democrats were to gain a majority in the Senate.

rows.source: Mkpesa kachasị ọhụrụ si na Florida Fish na Wildlife Commission na egosi mbelata zuru ọnụ na mbịakọta Mmiri Anụnụ maka akụkụ nke mpaghara Tampa Bay.

rows.source: Site na FWC, a na ekpesa ọnọdụ ntoju mpekere na mpaghara obere obodo nke Pinellas, Manatee, Sarasota, Charlotte na Collies - nke na atụnye mbịakọta na ebelata.
rows.output: From the FWC, the situation is being reported as a critical mass in the small urban areas of Pinellas, Manatee, Sarasota, Charlotte, and Collier counties - which includes a combination of manatees and eels.
